Serena Williams’s return to the US Open began with an opening round victory in the mixed doubles event before she and partner Carlos Alcaraz fell in the quarter-finals.

The all-star pairing beat Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool 5-3 4-1 in the first round before losing 5-4(7-4) 4-1 to fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli, while top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka crashed out in their opener.

Married pair ​Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina booked their place in the semi-finals with a thrilling win over doubles world No 1s Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten, winning a deciding tie-break after over an hour and a half on court.

They will face Bencic and Cobolli, while the all-Czech pairing of Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik will play either Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev or Diana Shnaider - Andreeva’s regular doubles partner - and Casper Ruud.

23-time major winner Williams had not competed ⁠at Arthur Ashe Stadium since her tearful farewell from the sport in 2022 and the crown jewel of American tennis erupted in deafening cheers as their queen took the court again.

The partisan crowd tried to keep Williams and Alcaraz in it as they were overpowered by Bencic and Cobolli, but they could not replicate their first-round exploits in a last-eight defeat.

The mixed doubles kicked off on Tuesday in the second year of ⁠its revamped format, which put singles stars in the spotlight in an effort to lure more fans in a standalone spot the week before the singles main draw.

open image in gallery ( Getty )

The move proved a commercial success in its debut year, drawing sellout crowds and attracting many of the sport's biggest singles names despite criticism from some doubles specialists, who argued it marginalised established pairings.

However this year the doubles specialists have struggled: nine players made it into the main draw but all lost before the semi-finals.

Djokovic and Sabalenka came unstuck against the experienced doubles players Patten and Siniakova, losing 1-4 4-2 10-2, as Siniakova sealed the match in style ‌with an ace out wide on match point, before the pair lost to Svitolina and Monfils in a high-quality clash.

Last year's champions, Italian duo Sara Errani ⁠and Andrea Vavassori, lost to Andreeva and Rublev 1-4 4-1 11-9 in the first round.

Additional reporting by Reuters

The high-profile mixed doubles event at the US Open is underway with several star pairings in action at Flushing Meadows.

Serena Williams, who returned to tennis in June, partnered up with defending men’s singles champion Carlos Alcaraz in New York – but the high-profile duo proved no match for Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the quarter-finals.

World No 1 women’s player Aryna Sabalenka and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic were the top seeds but lost in the first round, with the all-American pairing of Jessica Pegula and Taylor Fritz the second seeds.

The Italian doubles pairing of Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori were the defending champions, but also made an early exit.

Here’s everything you need to know for the US Open mixed doubles event.

When is it?

The main draw starts on Tuesday 25 August with the first round and quarter-finals. Play starts at 4pm BST (11am local) on Arthur Ashe Stadium and 3pm BST (10am local) on Louis Armstrong Stadium.

The semi-finals and final will headline a special night session on Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday 26 August, starting at midnight BST (7pm local).

What is the draw?

First round

Katerina Siniakova/Henry Patten bt. Aryna Sabalenka/Novak Djokovic [1] 1-4, 4-2, 2-10

Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils bt. Alexandra Eala/Felix Auger-Aliassime 4-1, 4-1

Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli [4] bt. Taylor Townsend/Alexander Zverev 4-2, 4-2

Serena Williams/Carlos Alcaraz bt. Erin Routliffe/Lloyd Glasspool 5-3, 4-1

Karolina Muchova/Jakub Mensik bt. Kristina Mladenovic/Marcelo Arevalo 4-1, 2-4, 10-7

Emma Navarro/Tommy Paul bt. Amanda Anisimova/Learner Tien [3] 5-3, 4-2

Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev bt. Sara Errani/Andrea Vavassori 1-4, 4-1, 11-9

Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud bt. Jessica Pegula/Taylor Fritz [2] 4-2, 4-1

Quarter-finals

Svitolina/Monfils bt Siniakova/Patten 5-4, 4-5, 10-8

Bencic/Cobolli [4] bt. Williams/Alcaraz 5-4, 4-1

Muchova/Mensik bt. Navarro/Paul 4-1, 5-3

Andreeva/Rublev vs Shnaider/Ruud

Semi-finals

Svitolina/Monfils vs Bencic/Cobolli [4]

Muchova/Mensik vs TBC

What is the format?

For every match up to the final, matches will be best-of-3 sets, with sets to four games and a 10-point tie-break instead of a third set.

For the final, it will be a traditional set to six games and a 10-point tie-break instead of a third set.

All matches will have sudden death deuce.

Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori won last year’s new-look mixed doubles event ( Getty )

Prize money

Round 1 (qualifying) - $10,000

Round 2 (qualifying) - $20,000

Round 1 (main draw) - $40,000

Quarter-finals - $120,000

Semi-finals - $250,000

Finalist - £500,000

Winner - $1,000,000

Where can I watch it?

Matches in the United Kingdom will be broadcast on Sky Sports Tennis.

In the United States, ESPN2 will present live coverage, with the final on ESPN and ESPN+.

Celtic threw away a four-goal lead in Austria as they missed out on the Champions League for the second year running.

The Scottish champions looked to be cruising into the league stage when Callum McGregor put them 4-0 up on aggregate against LASK with a 21st-minute deflected strike.

open image in gallery Celtic are out of the Champions League ( Reuters )

However, they went on to endure one of their all-time European lows with a 5-1 defeat in Linz delivering a £20m-plus blow.

The Hoops had other chances in the first half but the Austrians gave themselves a lifeline when Moses Usor pounced on a loose pass from Benjamin Nygren to level on the night in the 32nd minute.

The tie began to spiral out of Celtic’s control early in the second half as Robert Ljubicic and Samuel Adeniran netted from outside the box.

Martin O’Neill’s side looked like they would cling on but Florian Flecker nodded home from close range in stoppage-time to spark an additional 30 minutes.

open image in gallery LASK booked their spot in the league phase ( Getty )

Celtic had disappeared as an attacking force at half-time and Adeniran delivered the knockout blow that sends the Hoops into the Europa League.

The Hoops exited on penalties at the play-off stage last season after failing to sign a proven striker before drawing a blank against Kairat Almaty. Fans will this year question the decision to sell Arne Engels just ahead of the first leg after they lost control in midfield in Austria.

The quality of Celtic’s finishing had been the difference in Glasgow but LASK created chances throughout and the second leg started in similar fashion.

Celtic looked to extend their lead. Mika Baur stabbed an early chance just wide and Kasper Hogh forced a couple of first-half saves from decent opportunities.

McGregor opened the scoring in between those chances when he drilled a first-time shot in off a defender after Yang Hyun-jun had played a one-two with Kieran Tierney.

The home side had exerted some pressure just before McGregor’s goal and they levelled following careless play from Nygren.

open image in gallery LASK were relentless in the second leg ( Reuters )

The Austrian champions pulled a goal back three minutes after the restart when Usor out-muscled Auston Trusty and worked the ball inside for Ljubicic to drive home from 20 yards.

Celtic endured some nervy moments before they conceded again in the 58th minute when Adeniran curled a wonderful first-time strike into the top corner from 25 yards.

Celtic were on the ropes. Several shots flew past Viljami Sinisalo’s goal before the Finn pulled off a great stop from Sascha Horvath. Joao Victor Tornich headed inches wide from the resulting corner.

Adeniran fired off the underside of the bar and Celtic defended with four centre-backs as Liam Scales and Dane Murray came on to join Trusty and Cameron Carter-Vickers.

open image in gallery Martin O'Neill will be left to rue a horrible night in Linz ( Getty )

With Luke McCowan, Reo Hatate and Sebastian Tounekti also off the bench, Carter-Vickers had to struggle on with cramp and Celtic could not hold out. Sinisalo made a great stop from a Tornich header but Flecker converted the rebound.

Anthony Ralston replaced Carter-Vickers as extra-time allowed O’Neill to make an extra change and Celtic appeared to stem the tide.

However, Adeniran fired home from 25 yards with five minutes left after dispossessing McCowan and Celtic could not threaten after Sinisalo’s penalty save denied the striker his hat-trick.

PA

Dolly Parton liked to tell a story about the time she entered a Dolly Parton lookalike contest at a West Hollywood gay bar. “Me and a bunch of friends decided we’d go down there,” she recalled on a talk show in 2017. “They had these big drag queens, they looked great, prettier than I could ever dream of being. When they walked across the stage... whoever got the most applause won the contest. Here I come walking across the stage, and I got the least applause! So I always say, it’s terrible when [you’re Dolly Parton and you] lose a Dolly Parton lookalike contest!”

The Queen of Country’s death at the age of 80 has been announced by her family, sparking a global outpouring of grief. While she may have had a look that was easy to replicate, she was unquestionably one of a kind. A sharecropper’s daughter born in a two-room log cabin in rural Tennessee, her songwriting savvy and shrewd mind for business made her wealthy beyond her wildest dreams, with an estimated net worth of $500 million.

One of the most famous musicians on the planet, she was beloved across political and social divides: a self-made country music star and committed Christian who never forgot her Southern roots while championing LGBTQ rights, pouring money into childhood literacy programs and helping to fund a Covid vaccine.

Growing up “dirt poor” as the fourth of 12 children, Parton started singing in the local church at the age of six but later said she modeled her iconic look after “the town tramp”, despite the protestations of her father and a beating from her grandfather, a preacher.

“I didn’t know what she was, just this woman who was blond and piled her hair up, wore high heels and tight skirts, and, boy, she was the prettiest thing I'd ever seen,” Parton recalled. “Momma used to say, ‘Aw, she’s just trash,’ and I thought, ‘That’s what I want to be when I grow up. Trash.’” She maintained her larger-than-life image until her death, often quipping: “It takes a lot of money to look this cheap.”

open image in gallery Dolly Parton, seen here launching her album ‘Rockstar’ in Nashville in 2023, said she based her iconic look on ‘the town tramp’ ( Getty )

open image in gallery Dolly Parton, performing with Katy Perry and Kacey Musgraves in February 2019, inspired and collaborated with generations of singers and artists ( Getty )

Parton moved to Nashville to pursue her musical dreams the day after she graduated high school. That same day, while sitting outside the Wishy Washy Laundromat waiting for her laundry, she met a Nashville local who warned her she could get sunburned. That was Carl Dean, whom she married two years later in 1966.

They remained together for 59 years until his death in March 2025, and during that time were seen so rarely in public that fans began to speculate he might not even exist.

Parton, who described him as a “homebody and a loner”, wrote in her 1994 memoir that he had simply explained to her after his sole trip to a major music event shortly after their marriage that he preferred life out of the limelight. “I love you, and I will support you in your career any way I can,” Parton recalled him saying. “But I am not going to any more of these wingdings.”

Dean did, however, inspire countless of Parton’s songs. Most famously, it was a bank teller with eyes for Dean who inspired “Jolene”, the infectious 1973 country staple that became Parton’s signature anthem.

open image in gallery Dolly Parton is saluted by Keith Urban and Eric Church at the Nashville Songwriters Hall Of Fame Gala in October 2023 ( Getty )

“She got this terrible crush on my husband,” Parton told NPR in 2008. “And he just loved going to the bank because she paid him so much attention. It was kinda like a running joke between us — when I was saying, ‘Hell, you’re spending a lot of time at the bank. I don’t believe we’ve got that kind of money.’ So it’s really an innocent song all around, but sounds like a dreadful one.”

Her husband’s decision to avoid any contact with the press contributed to long-running rumors about Parton having affairs with her collaborators, stories she didn’t exactly outright deny.

“I’ve been accused of being involved with every man I’m ever seen with or worked with,” she told ABC News in 2012. “Maybe I have, maybe I ain’t. I never tell if I have. But you know people always saying that.”

She did however reject the suggestion that she was secretly in a lesbian relationship with her assistant and childhood friend, Judy Ogle, telling the New York Daily News that same year: “I’m not gay. If I was gay, I would have come out of the closet just a-flying.”

open image in gallery Dolly Parton and Carl Dean, who were married for almost 59 years ( Instagram/Dolly Parton )

So little was known about Parton’s life offstage that another persistent rumor centered on her penchant for outfits that, while skintight, kept her body fully covered.

One theory claimed that she was covered neck-to-toe in tattoos. That wasn’t true, she told People in 2020, but over the years she did get inked once or twice to cover up surgical scars. “I do have some tattoos, that’s true, but they’re tasteful. I’m not a tattoo girl,” she said. “Ribbons and bows and butterflies are the things that I have.”

“I was very sick for a while and I had to wear a feeding tube,” she added, referring to gynecological and digestive problems she faced in the early 1980s. “It left a little indentation in my side and I didn't like it because I’m so fair that scars turn purple on me. I like to make positives out of negatives. I had a little beehive tattooed over it — a little yellow-and-brown beehive with a tiny little bee on top of the hive. The mouth of it is that little sinkhole.”

She was open about her decision to undergo cosmetic surgery throughout her life, with a breast augmentation early in her career contributing to her signature look. She later had a breast reduction, as well as using Botox, fillers and having a number of facelifts. When health issues forced her to postpone a Las Vegas residency in 2025, she joked: “It must be time for my 100,000-mile check-up, although it’s not the usual trip to see my plastic surgeon!”

open image in gallery Dolly Parton accepted the Kennedy Center Honors from President George W Bush in 2006 (along with Smokey Robinson, Andrew Lloyd Webber, Steven Spielberg and Zubin Mehta), but later turned down the Presidential Medal of Freedom three times ( Getty )

Parton was more taciturn when it came to her political allegiances, never endorsing any specific candidates or parties. While she accepted the Kennedy Center Honors from President George W Bush in 2006, she later turned down the Presidential Medal of Freedom three times.

“I got offered the Freedom award from the Trump administration,” she told NBC in 2021. “I couldn’t accept it because my husband was ill, and then they asked me again about it and I wouldn’t travel because of the Covid.”

She explained that she was offered the prize once more by President Joe Biden, but again declined for fear of appearing to make a political statement. “Now I feel like if I take it, I’ll be doing politics, so I’m not sure,” she remarked. “I don’t work for those awards. It’d be nice, but I’m not sure that I even deserve it. But that’s a nice compliment for people to think that I might deserve it.”

She was equally modest when first approached about being inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. After being nominated in 2022, she attempted to withdraw, saying in a statement that: “I don’t feel that I have earned that right.”

She eventually acquiesced, and was inducted by Pink, but declared her intention to release a rock album in order to justify her inclusion. She followed through in 2023 by releasing Rockstar, an album that saw Parton covering songs by the likes of the Rolling Stones, Led Zeppelin and Queen, aided by guests including Beatles stars Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr, Stevie Nicks, Elton John and Blondie’s Debbie Harry.

open image in gallery Dolly Parton with the singer Pink being inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, after initially turning the honor down. She later released a rock’n’roll album, 2023’s ‘Rockstar’ ( Getty )

“I wanted it to be good, because I wanted rock artists to hear it and say, ‘Well, you know, that ain’t bad!’” Parton told The Independent at the time. She added that she had actually considered recording a rock album years ago, “but then I started getting older and I thought, bah, maybe I need to move on, ’cos nobody’s gonna take me serious.”

After the Rock Hall came calling, she reconsidered. “I thought it turned out really well,” she said. “I’m proud of it!”

It came as little surprise that so many of rock’s biggest names lined up to make music with Parton. She collaborated with a diverse range of artists throughout her career, earning some of her earliest hits with her country music mentor Porter Wagoner and recording with peers such as Willie Nelson and Kenny Rogers, a union which produced the huge 1983 hit “Islands In The Stream”.

open image in gallery Dolly Parton with fellow country icon and collaborator Willie Nelson in 2001 ( Getty )

In 1994 she duetted with Spanish crooner Julio Iglesias on “When You Tell Me That You Love Me”, and in recent years worked with a host of younger musicians from across several genres who all looked up to her.

She sang with Beyoncé on country crossover record Cowboy Carter, an album that also saw the former Destiny’s Child star offer up her own take on “Jolene”, and appeared on a remix of Sabrina Carpenter’s “Please Please Please”. She worked frequently with Miley Cyrus, who she had known since she was a child after Billy Ray Cyrus asked her to be his daughter’s godmother. The pair were also distant cousins, and Cyrus told W Magazine in 2024 that Parton had been “like a mother to me.”

open image in gallery Dolly Parton performing with Miley Cyrus, her goddaughter, in 2019. Cyrus said Parton was ‘like a mother to me’ ( Getty )

Parton’s influence extended far beyond just the music industry. After working on the 1980 workplace comedy 9 to 5 with Jane Fonda, the pair began a friendship they maintained until her death.

In 2017, Fonda recalled being taken on a trip to the Ozarks to drink moonshine with Parton’s cousin. “She taught me how to put your thumb in the jug and hoist it up, and I didn’t know I was drunk,” said Fonda with a laugh. “I was drunk for 10 days and I didn’t know it until I got home!”

Their friendship also had a serious side. In 2022, they appeared together in the documentary Still Working 9 to 5, which reflected on their subversive and trailblazing film in the light of the workplace and pay inequalities that still persisted more than four decades later.

open image in gallery Dolly Parton, Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin, seen here in 2006, remained firm friends after the success of their film ‘9 to 5’. They later worked on the documentary ‘Still Working 9 to 5’ ( Getty )

“People are still working their nine-to-five jobs, and women are still trying to find their equal pay and their equal importance, and I'm all about that,” Parton told NBC when the film was released. “I’m proud of the documentary and I hope it goes well.”

As much as she avoided labelling herself as a political figure, it was always evident that Parton was determined to use her good fortune to be a positive force in the world.

She raised millions for numerous good causes, including the American Red Cross and several HIV/Aids-related charities, and was involved in charitable campaigns ranging from relief from wildfires in the Great Smoky Mountains to the American Eagle Foundation’s efforts to preserve the bald eagle.

She was also a prolific businesswoman, with a diverse range of successful business ventures including TV specials, frozen food and her own Dollywood theme park in Tennessee. Among various rides and attractions, the park features a replica of the tiny log cabin where she was born.

open image in gallery Dolly Parton meeting schoolchildren in Rotherham during the launch of the UK's first Imagination Library. She told The Independent she wanted to be remembered as ‘someone who brought books to children all over the world’ ( Getty )

Her proudest achievement, however, was her Dollywood Foundation’s Imagination Library. The scheme mails a new, free book to children from around the world, from their birth until they begin kindergarten.

Parton, who never had children herself, funded the project in memory of her father. “My own father didn’t get a chance to go to school,” she told CNN in 2016. “He couldn't read and write, and that hindered him a great deal because he was so smart. It really bothered him a lot.”

At the time of her death, Parton’s Imagination Library was mailing books to almost 850,000 children each month in 1,600 communities across the U.S., Canada, the UK, Australia and the Republic of Ireland. In February 2018, Parton celebrated donating her 100 millionth free book.

“I want to be remembered as somebody who took her work serious, but not herself,” she told The Independent, when asked about her legacy. “Someone who brought books to children all over the world. For the fact that I managed to make a living doing something I love to do. And as a caring, giving, working girl.”

She’ll be remembered as all of that, and much more besides. She earned it. As she sang on 2008’s “Somebody’s Everything”: “All I want is everything, is that too much to ask?”

News.title: Michigan AG reveals state’s final accountability step for Flint water crisis
News.content:

Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel stated that a report published Tuesday regarding the Flint lead-water crisis represents the last measure her office can pursue toward establishing accountability. The release follows a state Supreme Court decision years prior that dismissed criminal charges against a former governor along with eight other individuals.

Flint residents endured years of health issues after lead leached from aging pipes into municipal drinking water when authorities switched to drawing from the Flint River to save money in 2014. The majority of the 101-page document outlines the background of the disaster, the delayed reaction from local and state officials and previous attempts to bring 42 felony and misdemeanor charges against nine people, including former Republican Gov. Rick Snyder.

Nessel, a Democrat currently in her final term, noted the publication provides a comprehensive public record of the criminal probe, expressing regret that the evidence was never heard by juries.

open image in gallery Nessel said the report is meant to be a thorough public account of the criminal investigation ( Bill Pugliano/Getty Images )

“I hope this offering revealing the inner workings of our dedicated investigators and prosecutors who helmed this yearslong effort and the facts and evidence which guided them may tell one part of the story of the Flint water crisis, and put the truth in the hands of the people of Flint who deserve it the most,” Nessel said.

After taking office in 2019, Nessel fired a special prosecutor who had brought criminal charges and assembled a new team of attorneys to determine whether crimes were committed. That team ultimately brought charges against Snyder and other key officials, presenting their evidence to a judge who acted as a one-person grand jury.

The state Supreme Court threw out those charges in 2022, saying the judge had no power to issue indictments under the grand jury law.

Nessel was not involved in the criminal cases, deciding instead to focus on settling lawsuits against the state and wall herself off from the criminal investigation. But on Tuesday she defended prosecutors' decision to seek the charges directly from a judge, calling it “the smartest possible move” at the time. She also questioned the political implications of the ruling, noting three of the justices who joined the unanimous ruling were appointed by Snyder.

“I think it’s impossible to separate those things,” Nessel said.

Nessel said it was frustrating that “justice has evaded the people of Flint” and they will not get their day in criminal court to see officials be held accountable for the water crisis.

open image in gallery In 2020, a judge approved a $626 million settlement for Flint residents and others who were exposed to lead-contaminated water ( Jeff Kowalsky/AFP via Getty Images )

The Associated Press sent an email Tuesday seeking comment from Snyder.

Prosecutors said in 2023 that a report would come out the following year summarizing their investigation. Nessel said it took more time to redact information from grand jury proceedings that must remain secret and summarize millions of other documents.

Cash-strapped Flint was under state financial control when it stopped getting its water from Detroit and began drawing it from the Flint River while waiting to connect to a new regional system. The move was made to save money. But chemicals used to treat the river water caused lead to leach from old pipes.

As state health officials said the water was safe, doctors started reporting high levels of lead in the blood of Flint children.

Snyder acknowledged the lead problem in September 2015, leading the state to provide water filters and testing of water in Flint schools. In early 2016, he declared a state of emergency in Flint. Congress eventually approved a bill authorizing water projects nationwide. About $170 million went to Flint to address lead in the drinking water.

In 2020, a judge approved a $626 million settlement for Flint residents and others who were exposed to lead-contaminated water. The Flint water crisis prompted other communities across the state and in other states to seek solutions to how drinking water was delivered to homes and businesses.

News.title: Carabao Cup: Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest
News.content:
James Trafford became the most expensive British goalkeeper in history this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start for Daniel Farke’s side and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No. 1” was the chant from the travelling Leeds fans and while it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice goalkeeper he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves while goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable night for Leeds, who won here in the Premier League on Saturday.

Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of them. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this avenue is now closed.

Four-time League Cup winners Forest endured a difficult evening despite the pre-match news that they have thrashed out a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

More to follow...

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

Sports.title: Ipswich star Marcelino Nunez scores from halfway line as Leicester’s misery continues in Carabao Cup defeat
Sports.content:
IPSWICH star Marcelino Nunez scored from the halfway line to compound yet more misery on pitiful Leicester City.

The Tractor Boys led 2-1 heading into injury time at Portman Road in round two.



And Nunez confirmed their place in the hat for the third round with a sensational strike.

The Chilean collected the ball in the centre circle just inside the Leicester half.





He spotted Foxes goalkeeper Jakub Stolarczyk off his line and let fly.

And his perfect lob caught Stolarczyk out, clipped the bar on its way in and bounced over the line.

The goal was not dissimilar to Abdul Fatawu’s astonishing effort for Leicester against Ipswich in the Championship last season.

The Ghana international then left relegated Foxes for the promoted Ipswich to return to the Premier League.



Nunez had earlier restored the lead for Gary O’Neil’s side with a neat finish off the post after Olebade Aluko’s first professional goal cancelled out Sindre Walle Egeli’s 62nd-minute opener.

Fans were loving the wondergoal on social media.

Sports.title: James Maddison suffers fractured shoulder in Tottenham’s horror defeat to Brentford as injury update issued
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM midfielder James Maddison has suffered a fractured shoulder.

Maddison, 29, missed almost all of last season after and ACL tear.



And the unlucky playmaker was crocked yet again in the horror opening day defeat to Brentford.

Maddison came on as a 68th-minute sub in the mauling at the Gtech.



But he was in the wars immediately and Spurs confirmed that an MRI scan has shown a slight fracture after an awkward fall during the game.

Maddison initially hurt his ACL at the end of the 24/25 season.

READ MORE ON FOOTBALL DRUG RAP Sterling charged with dangerous driving & possessing laughing gas after car crash

He attempted to come back during the following pre-season, but suffered a full rupture in the process.

He finally returned to action in May as he went on to make three appearances to help Tottenham avoid relegation.

The England international was also limited during pre-season due to a minor issue.

But there is hope that he will not spend too long on the sidelines as head coach Roberto De Zerbi labelled this latest setback as a “small injury.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Maddison was able to take part in limited training on Monday.

And it is hoped he will return before next month’s extended international break.

It is a relief for Tottenham as injuries continue to trouble the club after their 17th-placed finish last season.

Both Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are currently sidelined with long-term ACL injuries.

Dejan Kulusevski and Mohammed Kudus are also out of action with knee and quad injuries, respectively.



While new captain Micky van de Ven and Pape Matar Sarr also did not feature against Brentford.

But Spurs have been boosted by the £85million deal to sign Savinho from Manchester City – with Oumar Marmoush set to follow next.

De Zerbi’s side will next host Newcastle at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday, August 29.

Sports.title: Epic Wolverhampton Wanderers-themed boozer wins Pub Shed of the Year award leaving owners ‘gobsmacked’
Sports.content:
A COUPLE have won Pub Shed of the Year for their Wolverhampton Wanderers- themed boozer.

Tina and Rich Hibbs have spent £25,000 over eight years crafting the backyard bolthole.



Packed with Wolves shirts and memorabilia, it boasts a bar with draught lager and cider, TV, Pac-Man machine and beer garden.

Baker Tina, 48, of Rugeley, Staffs, said: “We have a friend who runs a business making these, so he helped with the shell while the interior was all done by us.



“It has become a great space for entertaining.

“Every Easter we do an egg hunt and we decorate it all up for Halloween.



“We also have our Christmas dinner in there, I usually cater for about 15 people each year.

“Our friends love it.



“I’m not sure about our neighbours but we’ve not had any complaints!”

The couple were “gobsmacked” by the award and celebrated after retired skip firm boss Rich, 57, returned from Wolves’ 3-1 win at Preston.

Tina added: “It’s become a great space for entertaining.”

Award organisers Two Fat Blokes bar signs and Ngage Radio said: “Hibby’s Bar is a worthy winner.”

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and possessing laughing gas after crashing £270k Lambo
Sports.content:
FORMER Premier League ace Raheem Sterling could get two years’ jail if convicted of dangerous driving after his £270,000 Lamborghini M-way crash.

The ex-England winger, 31, has also been charged with possessing laughing gas and failing to provide a specimen following his arrest in May.



Motorists dialled 999 after seeing a black luxury 4×4 swerving across the M3 in Hampshire just before 9am.

The former Liverpool, Man City and Chelsea winger was arrested close to an interchange near Farnborough.



Sterling, who is currently without a club, had been due to answer bail on Friday.

He will now appear before magistrates in Basingstoke on September 15, police revealed yesterday.



A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.

“Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

“The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.

“No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported.



“Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September.”

Nitrous oxide, also known as laughing gas and hippy crack, was made illegal when reclassified as a class C controlled substance in November 2023.

Usage is rife among footballers, despite its dangers including risk of heart attacks, stroke and brain damage.

It typically comes in supersized canisters used to fill balloons, which are then inhaled repeatedly to give a euphoric, short-lived high.

Sterling was just 15 when he was signed by Liverpool from the QPR academy in 2010.



He became a fans’ favourite at Anfield before a contract dispute saw him move to Manchester City in 2015.

There he enjoyed massive success — winning four Premier League titles, five Carabao Cups and an FA Cup.

However, sources close to Sterling told how his mental health suffered following his £50million transfer from Man City to Chelsea in July 2022.



He was eventually ordered to train separately to the first-team group after then-manager Enzo Maresca — now Man City boss — decided he was surplus to requirements.

A loan deal to Arsenal followed, but did not work out, so in February he joined Dutch club Feyenoord.

That deal ended in the summer and he is now without a club.



Sources also claimed he has been written off and made to feel “worthless” despite gaining 82 England caps.

One said: “He was a prolific international who steered the England squad to significant heights over the last decade and has been made to feel worthless.

“The psychological strain that has put on him is immeasurable.

“He feels isolated.

“The second he touches a ball, he’s told he’s a flop and he’s finished.



“He’s been mocked and heckled.

“He moved to the Netherlands to escape and rediscover his love for the game, but the negativity followed.

“It’s been extremely tough.”

Since the M3 incident, Sterling has kept a low profile and has rarely been pictured, apart from social media footage of him playing football with his children.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He is engaged to childhood sweetheart Paige Milian, 30, with whom he has two kids.



He also has a daughter from a previous relationship.

Sports.title: Green-fingered Jack Grealish wins planning battle to change wood at £5.6m pad into garden to indulge veg-growing hobby
Sports.content:
FOOTIE ace Jack Grealish is singing Come On You Greens after winning a planning fight to change woodland behind his mansion into a garden where he can grow vegetables.

The Man City star had been in a battle to have ten acres of his grounds declared garden land.



Green-fingered Grealish told planners he had grown veg since moving into the £5.6million Cheshire pile he shares with girlfriend Sasha Attwood and daughter Mila Rose in 2023.

He said in a planning application: “The garden spaces are used for exercising our dog and we grow vegetables in the allotment areas.”



After months of wrangling the 30-year-old has been given a “positive certificate” to continue using the land as a garden, despite objections that the move could lead to further building projects on it.

England international Grealish is following former Three Lions skipper David Beckham by growing vegetables.

Making its decision, Cheshire East Council says in a report: “The current owner has owned the house since 2022 and has included a declaration of use of the land as garden.

“On the balance of probability it has been demonstrated that the land . . . has been used as residential garden for more than ten years before the date of this application.”

The parish council had objected — saying if the woodland was classed as garden, it would pave the way for future planning applications.

It says a similar 2022 application by the previous owner was denied.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes defying docs was catalyst to Man Utd’s resurgence under Carrick – but he needs a title for legend status
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES’ PFA Player of the Year crown is a staggering achievement at a club that has frequently looked lost.

But let’s be clear: without Fernandes’ profound influence at Manchester United, Michael Carrick would not be in a job today.



Fernandes was the catalyst for United’s resurgence under Carrick last season.

When United faced Manchester City in Carrick’s first game, they were desperate for a breakthrough.



It was Fernandes’ breathtaking precision, carrying a counter-attack from deep within his own half before releasing a perfectly timed pass to Bryan Mbeumo, that put United 1-0 up in a game they won 2-0.

That moment sparked an incredible run of 12 wins in 17 games, turning United’s season completely on its head.



Crucially, his availability that week was a minor miracle in itself.

Having suffered a hamstring injury against Aston Villa that club medics warned would keep any ordinary player out for a month, Fernandes’ unrivalled pain threshold — the highest Carrington medical staff have ever known — saw him defy science to return in a fortnight.

Without him bailing them out, Carrick’s reign would likely have been over before it even began.

Yet, to truly cement his place in club folklore, Fernandes had to overcome the prominence of two of the club’s biggest players: Cristiano Ronaldo and Harry Maguire.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It is no secret that Fernandes’ weakest season at Old Trafford was Ronaldo’s first year back – he looked cowed, subservient, and largely stifled by Ronaldo’s towering presence.

Meanwhile, Harry Maguire’s struggling form hung like a shadow over the squad.

The defining moment of Fernandes’ captaincy arrived when Erik ten Hag ruthlessly dropped both Ronaldo and Maguire simultaneously before facing Liverpool, handing Fernandes the armband.

Fernandes set a ferocious tone, United won, and he finally broke the shackles to become the undisputed, vocal leader of the club.

Most opposition fans despise Fernandes.



On the pitch, he is the ultimate pantomime villain – a whiny, hand-waving demon who milks challenges, dabbles in theatrics, and aggressively appeals for phantom fouls like he did just days ago against Hull City.

But talk to anyone behind the scenes at Carrington, and the contrast is astounding.

Away from the cameras, Bruno is a Fernandes is warm company and mild-mannered. He has struck up genuine friendships with unsung staff members, even meeting up with one who was made redundant.



While highly paid superstars come and go, those at Carrington fiercely protect Fernandes because of how deeply he respects them.

He is a complex, Jekyll-and-Hyde character: a whining demon on the pitch, but an eloquent, loyal leader off it.

Yet, despite winning both the PFA and FWA gongs, where does Fernandes truly sit in the pantheon of Old Trafford greatness? For all his world-class consistency, it’s clear to me that he remains a “club great” rather than a “club legend.”

I have long insisted that the hallowed title of Manchester United legend must be reserved for the elite few who actually delivered league titles — names like Best, Charlton, Cantona, and Ronaldo.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Until Fernandes can spearhead a genuine Premier League title win, his legacy remains tantalisingly incomplete.



Now, as he takes home the PFA title once more, United must celebrate their talisman — and Michael Carrick should raise the biggest glass of all to the man who saved his career.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes WINS PFA players’ player of the year to become first Man Utd star in 16 years to land coveted award
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES has delivered a clean sweep of awards after being voted the PFA players’ player of the year.

The Manchester United midfielder picked up the Premier League and FWA awards last season.



And he pipped the likes of Declan Rice and Erling Haaland to the PFA award, which was voted for by his fellow top-flight stars.

Manchester City’s Nico O’Reilly won the young player of the year award at Manchester Opera House.



Five of the title-winning Arsenal team got in the Premier League team of the year.

Fernandes, 31, has been outstanding since arriving from Sporting Lisbon for £47million in 2020.

He has become the first United player since Wayne Rooney in 2010 to win the PFA award.

The Portuguese international was rewarded for a string of outstanding performances for United – even though they did not win any silverware – and he set a Premier League record of 21 assists.

He was level on 20 assists with Arsenal’s Thierry Henry and Manchester City’s Kevin de Bruyne before taking the record against Brighton on the final day of the season.

He set up Patrick Dorgu’s opener in a 3-0 win which saw him score a ninth goal of the season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fernandes had already written himself into United’s history books, surpassing David Beckham’s title as the club’s top creator.

Beckham previously held the club’s record for the most assists in a single Premier League season, setting up 15 goals in the 1999/2000 campaign.

Fernandes, who received the award from former United midfielder Juan Mata, said: “It’s a very proud moment.

“Obviously, I’m very thankful for all of those that voted for me.

“It was a special season individually for me, and I’m very proud that all the players have decided to vote for me. I am very, very grateful.”



On his assist record, Fernandes added: “I hadn’t thought much about it until you guys started commenting so much.

“Obviously, then when I started getting closer, I started thinking about it and everything.

“But I think it got more into my strikers, because they were so eager to score the goal and to give me that assist, that sometimes they even forgot about their own game.



“But I am very happy, because assisting means that someone is getting goals.

“Obviously, we don’t play tennis, that we play for just ourselves, we play football.

“We play for the team, we play for a club, we play for our fans and there’s nothing more special than that.”



Asked if he is optimistic for the season after the Hull defeat, the United captain responded: “We’ve got a game at home that we want to win, and it is as simple as that.

“We are not thinking too much about the ones that have gone.”

At the awards ceremony, Hayden Hackney – now at Everton – was announced as the Championship player of the year for his exploits with Middlesbrough.

Orient striker Dom Ballard won the League One award although he has since moved to Bristol City.

Swindon forward Aaron Drinan took the League Two trophy.



Manchester City’s Bunny Shaw won the women’s player of the year.

Players are now only allowed to vote for the award in the division where they play.

The PFA now stages the ceremony at the start of the season, meaning players are able to vote until June.

Previously, the deadline was April for the May ceremony, meaning the season had not been completed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney also picked up merit awards in Manchester for their contributions to the game.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup 2026/27 round dates: When are 3rd round matches played?
Sports.content:
FANS are dreaming of a trip to Wembley in the Carabao Cup.

Manchester City won the trophy last year, beating Arsenal 2-0 in the final.



The nine Premier League teams playing in Europe enter the competition in round three, with the others in the hat from round two.

SunSport bring you all the key dates for your diary this year.



Carabao Cup 2026/27 round dates

Round One: Weekend of 7-9 August 2026

Round Two: w/c 24 August 2026

Round Three: w/c 7 September and w/c 14 September 2026

Round Four: w/c 26 October 2026

Round Five: w/c 14 December 2026

Semi-Final First Leg: w/c 11 January 2027

Semi-Final Second Leg: w/c 1 February 2027

Final: Sunday 21 March 2027

Is there extra-time in the Carabao Cup 2026/27?

There is no extra-time in the Carabao Cup until the semi-final.

All ties before the last four go straight to penalties if level after 90 minutes.



But if the score is level on aggregate at the end of the two-legged semi-final, an extra 30 minutes will be played with no away goals rule.

That will be followed by penalties if there is still nothing to seperate them.

This is the same with the final at Wembley.

Sports.content:
Arsenal transfer target Julian Alvarez nears point of no return at Atletico Madrid

Arsenal are ready to pull the trigger on a blockbuster £130million transfer for Julian Alvarez - but only if the wantaway star is ready to give up on a move to Barcelona

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez's future will finally be decided in the coming days (Image: Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez is nearing the point of no return at Atletico Madrid - but Arsenal are facing a race against time to get a deal done.

‌



The Argentina star, 26, was booed by Atletico fans last weekend after making it clear he wants to leave the club with Barcelona his preferred choice. That has caused a major row with the hierarchy behind the scenes and there may be no way back for the want-away striker with the next few days crucial in resolving Alvarez’s future and whether Atletico decide to stay firm or sell.

‌



Arsenal are ready to pounce if they are given encouragement by Atletico or Alvarez but the clock is ticking to get a mega deal done before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday night.

The Gunners will have to bid around £130m to tempt Atletico to sell and they will also want to know that Alvarez is fully committed because he made it clear that he wants to join Barcelona.

Sports.title: Why Tottenham's £85m swoop for Savio just doesn't add up - except for Man City
Sports.content:
Why Tottenham's £85m swoop for Savio just doesn't add up - except for Man City

Rafi Moersen was the brains behind City's decision to sign Brazilian flop Savio - and has now done it again on behalf of Spurs - for £50m more in a deal which is difficult to fathom

View 2 Images Savinho has cost Tottenham a staggering £85m (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Senior figures at Manchester City are said to be thrilled with the sale of Savio to Tottenham in a deal which could reach £85m.

‌



And so they should be. Because somehow, City have managed to make more than £50m profit on a footballer who contributed little or nothing to the team's success in the short time he spent at the Etihad.

‌



It took Pep Guardiola less than half a season to realise he'd made a mistake in signing the Brazilian winger from Troyes in 2024. In two seasons in Manchester, Savio made just 28 league appearances. These included a grand total of seven last season. But it was his lack of commitment as much as his lack of impression and goals, which made the £30.8m fee look extortionate.

‌



Let's just say Guardiola and his coaching staff had little time for Savio's work rate and reluctance to get physical when he needed to. But there is a man working at the highest level of football who must see something in Savinho no-one else can: Carlos Raphael Moersen.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Moersen, who is known as 'Rafi" to his friends and colleagues, oversaw Savio's transfer to City when he was the City Football Group executive.

‌



He spent almost a decade working across CFG clubs and, and was responsible for overseeing football transactions within the organisation. In December of 2025 Moersen was lured to Tottenham, as the club's new director of football operations. Moersen arrived in north London with big ideas.

And it just so happens one of them was for Spurs to sign Savio. Which they have now done. Signing someone who looks out of his depth in the Premier League once, is clumsy. But doing the same thing twice is downright foolish. Undeterred, Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi is under the impression he's landed himself a game-changing star.

View 2 Images Savinho failed to make an impact at Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Savio is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity," he said.

Spurs' fascination with Savio is as remarkable as it is hard to fathom. Because, and with respect to De Zerbi, if Guardiola didn't rate him, then why would an Italian whose greatest managerial achievement to date is winning the Ukrainian Super Cup?

Spurs supporters should be bracing themselves. To witness a footballer who flatters to deceive - thus personifying what his new club have been all about in recent times.

Sports.title: Leeds earn second win at Forest in three days in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Leeds United registered a second win at Nottingham Forest in three days as they booked their spot in the Carabao Cup third round.

Daniel Farke's side took the three Premier League points home on Saturday and earned a 2-0 victory in the League Cup thanks to goals from Dan James and James Justin.

Having not won at the City Ground since 1972 before the weekend, they have now triumphed there twice in 72 hours as the Yorkshire club enjoy a winning start to the new campaign.

It is not the start new Forest boss Oliver Glasner was looking for as things are yet to click, though additions are on the way with a £50m deal agreed for Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Neither side will have been jumping for joy at the prospect of a rematch so soon after Saturday's Premier League opener.

But Forest enjoyed some early promise as James Trafford was forced into a great save in the 10th minute when he had to fend away Ola Aina's cross-shot, which almost left him wrongfooted.

Then Justin was in the right place at the right time to stop Igor Jesus' header from going in.

Leeds came into it and should have gone in front midway through the first half when James got in down the right, but his pull-back was just behind Sean Longstaff, who shot straight at Matz Sels.

Image: James Justin scores Leeds' second goal at Forest

Both sides were going for it and Leeds defender Joe Rodon denied Chris Wood with a brilliant last-ditch tackle while Sels kept out James' low effort at the other end.

The Wales international showed the required composure five minutes after the restart.

Aina's wayward header allowed Longstaff to gallop forward and he played in James, who clipped home.

Forest almost hit straight back as Arnaud Kalimuendo's cutback was perfect for Wood, but Trafford did brilliantly to stop his effort from going into the bottom corner, before Noah Okafor sent an effort just wide as Leeds staged a rapid counter-attack.

Leeds sealed the victory with 15 minutes remaining but there was nothing pretty about it.

Lucas Nmecha tried to claim it as his bundled effort was blocked on the line by Williams, with Justin finally putting the ball into the back of the net.

Sports.title: Wilson scores on full debut as Brentford hit Birmingham for six
Sports.content:
Callum Wilson scored just six minutes into his full debut and captain Nathan Collins converted two headers as Brentford routed Championship side Birmingham 6-1.

The 34-year-old Wilson, who joined on a free transfer from relegated West Ham, seized his first opportunity with a crisp finish which took a deflection off defender Dael Fry, who had a debut to forget.

Brentford's Premier League quality was evident throughout and although Blues equalised through Demarai Gray just before the half-hour they were level for just seven minutes.

Image: Callum Wilson scored six minutes into his full Brentford debut

Lax defending saw Aaron Hickey and Collins score in quick succession to effectively seal the tie before half-time, with Mikkel Damsgaard getting on the end of a counter-attack to add the fourth.

Igor Thiago's smart close-range finish sent fans streaming for the exit, missing Collins' second header.

The Bees, quarter-finalists last season, had not beaten Birmingham in six previous meetings, the last a goalless draw more than five years ago in the Championship before they went on to bigger and better things which their ambitious hosts now hope to emulate.

Birmingham's priority remains promotion so, after opening with two league draws, boss Chris Davies made six changes, including goalkeeper Ryan Allsop, Fry and Argentinian striker Luis Vazquez.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Callum Wilson produced a composed finish to put Brentford ahead just six minutes into his first competitive start for the club.

However, the gulf to a Premier League squad was evident as Keith Andrews retained only three of the team which demolished Tottenham and saw three of his newcomers score and another, Yehor Yarmoliuk, run the midfield before he was forced off with injury.

Davies wants to meet the club's aspirations by playing their way out of the Championship but it proved their undoing before they had even had chance to get a foothold in the game as they fell foul of Brentford's high press at a short goal-kick.

Paik Seung-ho was slow to react to the loose ball and Yarmoliuk played in Wilson to fire home first-time from the edge of the area with the aid of a deflection.

But a miscontrol by Jannik Schuster saw the centre-back booked for bringing down Vazquez and from Paik's short free-kick Gray drilled a deflected shot through a crowd of players.

It was a brief moment of joy in an otherwise chastening night as a failure to deal with Vitaly Janelt's chip and Wilson's strength allowed Hickey to fire home an angled shot.

Collins jumped in front of Fry to nod in a simple header from Jaidon Anthony's cross but a ruthless Brentford went for the kill and, after bringing on the likes of Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Mamadou Sangare, scored three more after the break.

The managers...

Birmingham's Chris Davies:

"My message to supporters tonight is 'sorry'. It's not very pleasant and I can understand how frustrating it is for them.

"It was a very tough evening for us, a painful evening, and incredibly disappointing to lose a game 6-1 at home.

"There were many situations where we were just not good enough to compete and I take ultimate responsibility for it - and the players will have to do it in their own minds.

"We were beaten by a team a long way ahead of us in every aspect. Was 6-1 a fair reflection? Probably."

Brentford's Keith Andrews:

"I didn't really blink an eyelid making so many changes.

"There is a huge narrative around cup games with coaches making changes but with the squad we have, there are fine margins between who plays and doesn't play.

"We needed to compete really hard to play the game we wanted. I thought overall we produced a really good performance."

Sports.title: Coventry survive Plymouth scare to progress in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Premier League new boys Coventry survived an EFL Cup second-round scare at League One Plymouth before easing through 4-2 at Home Park.

City had showed their class by racing into a 2-0 lead within five minutes courtesy of goals from Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni but Argyle fought back to level nine minutes into the second half thanks to debutant Danny Irow and Xavier Amaechi.

Second-half substitute Ephron Mason-Clark scored City's third goal within five minutes of his 62nd-minute introduction before Victor Torp wrapped things up with a 78th-minute penalty.

Awoniyi fired City ahead on three minutes, picking his spot after a brilliant flick-on by Caleb Yirenkyi.

Yirenkyi's sublime pass on the spin from skipper Liam Kitching's through ball set striker Awoniyi on his way to goal and he had time to pick his spot to beat home goalkeeper James Storer with a side foot finish.

Within two minutes City increased their lead following a lightning break down the right. Awoniyi set Rudoni racing on his way to goal and he made no mistake, again beating Storer with a clinical finish, this time from the edge of the box.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Coventry stunned Plymouth with a quick-fire double as Taiwo Awoniyi opened his account for the club before Jack Rudoni added a second moments later.

Jake Bidwell came close to making it 3-0 on the 18th minute, heading just past the post from Joel Latibeaudiere's pinpoint cross to the far post.

Argyle responded in the 21st minute through Irow, who cut in from the left and beat Latibeaudiere, before sending a low shot past City keeper Daniel Bentley into the far corner.

Midfielder Harvey White had sent Irow - who has just joined Plymouth on loan from Tottenham - away down the left with a superb pass from his own half after spotting the winger out wide.

The unmarked Awoniyi could have doubled his tally on 27 minutes but headed wide from six yards from Latibeaudiere's deep cross.

Striker Will Evans' effort flew off the foot of Bentley and on to a post in the 31st minute after the keeper had failed to hold White's long-range effort.

Argyle restored parity on 54 minutes when half-time sub Amaechi won the ball from City defender Kitching and raced into the box before beating Bentley with a thumping low drive into the corner.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto volleyed just over from Mason-Clark's cross in the 65th minute before the latter restored City's lead in the 67th minute from close range, turning in Torp's thumping cross.

Torp gave Coventry some breathing space by converting a penalty following a foul by sub Joe Edwards on Brandon Thomas-Asante, who could have increased City's lead in stoppage time but hammered his volley over from the edge of the six-yard box.

Sports.title: Hull require penalties to overcome stubborn Stoke
Sports.content:
Premier League new boys Hull followed up their 2-0 win over Manchester United on Saturday by knocking Stoke out of the Carabao Cup on penalties after a 1-1 draw at the bet365 Stadium.

Robert Bozenik opened the scoring for the hosts before the Tigers equalised through Kieran Dowell on the stroke of half time.

With neither side able to force a winner, Hull ran out 5-4 winners on penalties.

Sergej Jakirovic made 11 changes to the side that stunned Manchester United at the weekend, handing full debuts to Lucas Herrington and Matt Targett, as well as midfield pair Jens Hjerto-Dahl and Lucas Gourna-Douath.

It was a bright start from Hull, and Hjerto-Dahl in particular, who opened his body up and curled an effort towards the far post which was pushed wide by Josh Griffiths.

Paddy McNair then headed Liam Millar's corner wide at the back post as the visitors enjoyed the best of the opening exchanges.

After losing their opening two Championship games of the season, including a 2-1 defeat to Swansea at the bet365 Stadium on the opening day, Mark Robins made seven changes as Bozenik, Luke Graham, Ben Pearson, Tomas Rigo, Million Manhoef and Laurence Giani were all handed starts.

Stoke had reportedly turned down a bid from the Tigers for star winger Sorba Thomas, and it was the Wales international who created the opener when he cut in from the left and whipped a cross in that was met by Bozenik.

The Slovakian scored the only goal when the pair last met on New Year's Day, and the forward brushed aside McNair to head Stoke in front.

Griffiths had been given the nod in goal as Viktor Johansson was given the night off and the former West Brom stopper beat away Dowell's first effort from distance as half-time loomed.

But the former Rangers man wasn't to be denied a second time as he lashed home after he was picked out by Millar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kieran Dowell brings Hull level in their Carabao Cup clash with Stoke City.

David Akintola was making his first appearance for Hull since January and spurred two golden chances to put them ahead after the break.

The Nigerian firstly steered Targett's cross wide of the right-hand post before rounding Griffiths and firing into the side-netting after he was played in by Millar.

The forward then saw his next sight of goal comfortably saved by Griffiths.

With nothing to separate the sides at the end of 90 minutes, it was to be a penalty shootout that decided the tie.

New Stoke signing George Hirst saw his tame penalty kept out by Dillon Phillips, while Hull converted all five of their spot kicks as Mohamed Belloumi sent the Tigers into round three for the first time in six years.

Sports.title: West Ham hit back to thump four past Southampton
Sports.content:
Teenager Josh Ayala scored twice on his full professional debut as West Ham came from behind to thrash Championship rivals Southampton 4-1 in the Carabao Cup.

Nuno Espirito Santo made it clear a cup run was not his priority by fielding a team made up of four teenagers and three 20-year-olds among eight changes from Saturday's home defeat by Charlton.

Southampton took just 10 minutes to open the scoring. Tom Fellows' looping right-wing cross was cleared only to Leo Scienza on the edge of the penalty and he showed great composure to keep the ball under pressure before calmly slotting into the far bottom corner.

Image: Jarrod Bowen scored West Ham's fourth at St Mary's

Saints goalkeeper Daniel Peretz then made an excellent one-handed save to keep out Joel Piroe's close-range effort in the 21st minute.

West Ham equalised against the run of play four minutes before half-time when Peretz flapped at Lewis Orford's corner and 19-year-old Ayala headed home.

The Hammers took the lead eight minutes into the second half when Ayala cashed in on Jack Stephens' poor defending to fire past Peretz from eight yards.

Taty Castellanos swept in Joel Veltman's low cross 15 minutes from time before Jarrod Bowen grabbed an 84th minute fourth to condemn Southampton to a first home defeat since January 17.

The managers...

Southampton's Tonda Eckert:

"It was a very good first half and a very poor second from us.

"We had chances to go 2-0 up, conceded from a corner and from there we never found a way back into the game.

"There were some positives but as a team we need to grow and become better in a lot of different aspects."

West Ham's Nuno Espirito Santo:

"I am very proud of my young players and the character and belief they showed.

"It is important for Josh. He works hard every day in training to get chances in games. We are delighted he took the opportunity.

"We did not start very well but with these young lads we have to give them time and understand the process of their development.

"Winning breeds confidence and it is important now we build momentum from this and keep going."

Sports.title: Nunez's halfway stunner helps Ipswich past Leicester
Sports.content:
Marcelino Nunez scored a sensational goal from the halfway line to help Ipswich claim a hard-fought 3-1 win over Leicester in the Carabao Cup.

This had been a Premier League fixture only 15 months ago, but Leicester arrived at Portman Road fresh from a painful home loss to Burton in League One and yet under-fire Russell Martin watched the Foxes edge a goalless first half.

Sindre Walle Egeli showed Premier League quality for Gary O'Neil's team with a smart left-footed finish to break the deadlock after 62 minutes before 19-year-old Olabade Aluko earned Leicester a deserved leveller five minutes later.

However, ex-Norwich midfielder Nunez fittingly had the final say in the meeting between two former Canaries team-mates.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Marcelino Nunez scores from near the halfway line in stunning strike for Ipswich against Leicester in the Carabao Cup.

Nunez rifled home off a post after 71 minutes to score for the first time at Portman Road since his move last summer and added a wonderful 50-yard lob in stoppage time to help Ipswich reach the Carabao Cup third round for only the second time in 11 seasons.

Martin was booed after Leicester lost to Burton and watched his team almost gift an opener inside 33 seconds, but Chuba Akpom could not profit.

Leicester, to their credit, quickly settled and Brighton loanee Tom Watson sent one shot wide before he tested Christian Walton with a curled effort.

Ipswich back-up goalkeeper Walton thwarted Christian McFarlane's attempted chip in the 20th minute after a lovely Louis Page pass and at the other end Jakub Stolarczyk made a fine save from Dara O'Shea's header.

However, Leicester finished the half strongly when Conor Chaplin's curler was pushed wide by Walton.

Ipswich midfielder Kasey McAteer had a goal ruled out for offside two minutes after half-time before Chaplin was withdrawn to a standing ovation on the hour mark by Martin, who then watched the home side break the deadlock in the 62nd minute.

Akpom played through to Jack Clarke and he squared for Egeli to slot home.

Five minutes later, Leicester equalised when Page's corner was flicked on by Bobby De Cordova-Reid and 19-year-old Aluko got a faint touch to score his first professional goal.

Nunez ensured there would be no upset when he fired in via a post after Woyo Coulibaly had given the ball away and after Akpom squandered a one-on-one chance, the Chile international grabbed a second.

After the ball dropped inside the centre circle, Nunez spotted Stolarczyk off his line and lobbed over the Leicester goalkeeper in incredible fashion to make it back-to-back wins for O'Neil.
