Sports.title: Victor Torp seals Coventry’s Carabao Cup win at Plymouth in six-goal thriller
Sports.content:
A midweek trip to Devon always had the makings of an awkward trip for a Coventry side focused on Premier League survival. Such feelings evaporated when Frank Lampard’s side raced into a two-goal lead inside five minutes, Taiwo Awoniyi opening his account for his new club before Jack Rudoni added Coventry’s second. But, ultimately, Coventry were made to toil before earning victory.

Plymouth had form for a cup upset and another was brewing when Xavier Amaechi pulled Tom Cleverley’s side level nine minutes into the second half. Coventry, to their credit, roused once more, the substitute Ephron Mason-Clark regaining the lead before Victor Torp sealed progress to the Carabao Cup third round from the penalty spot.

As Gustavo Hamer, one of nine changes from the Coventry team that began Friday’s defeat at Arsenal, took kick-off, the visitors’ intentions were clear. The centre-backs Liam Kitching, captain for the night, and Bobby Thomas, were the only players not to start on the halfway line and Coventry quickly got to work. Thomas and Caleb Yirenkyi were the only players retained from the XI that opened their Premier League campaign and the latter’s sumptuous first-time flick from Kitching’s pass freed Awoniyi in on goal inside three minutes. Awoniyi applied a cool side-foot finish and there were only four minutes and six seconds on the clock when Awoniyi turned provider, releasing Rudoni to double Coventry’s advantage.

At that point, the 2,100 Coventry supporters, many of whom made an eight-hour, 444-mile round trip, cycled through the back catalogue of songs. Then Lampard obliged when they craved a wave from a manager who led them back to the top flight after 25 years away. But the game did not turn the non-event most would have envisaged and instead an absorbing cup tie unfolded. Cleverley accepted the game, for his team, was “a little bit of a free hit, nothing to lose”.

And Plymouth were suddenly liberated. Mathias Ross sent a free header wide from a free-kick and a couple of minutes later Irow read Harvey White’s flighted pass and the Tottenham loanee, 24 hours after signing, drove inside Joel Latibeaudiere and drilled past Dan Bentley, the Coventry goalkeeper on debut. From there, aside from Awoniyi heading wide unmarked, Coventry had to withstand plenty of Plymouth pressure and the hosts should have restored parity just after the half hour. Bentley fumbled White’s speculative shot from outside the box and Evans pounced on the rebound but Bentley managed to divert Evans’s shot on to his left post.

View image in fullscreen Jack Rudoni doubles Coventry’s lead from close range in the fifth minute. Photograph: Dan Mullan/Getty Images

Aurèle Amenda replaced Thomas at the interval. For Cleverley, this was also a touchline duel with a friend and a former England teammate. “All the young English coaches want people like Frank to do well … not tomorrow night but moving forward the English coaches are right behind people like Frank and Michael [Carrick] at Man Utd,” Plymouth’s head coach said on the eve of the game.

Cleverley knew the value of recording an upset, Lampard the damage of defeat. Rudoni sent a fizzing first-time effort narrowly wide from Awoniyi’s smart layoff a few minutes into the second half but Amaechi, who replaced Caleb Watts at half-time, levelled on 54 minutes. Ameachi swarmed Kitching, pinching the ball after the Coventry defender got in a tangle and then fired a left-foot shot in at Bentley’s near post. Plymouth freshened things up with a triple substitution, including the homegrown academy graduates Tegan Finn and Caleb Roberts.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Lampard, meanwhile, turned to Mason-Clark, this his first appearance of the season after a hamstring issue. It was a galling goal from a Plymouth perspective. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s cross from the right caused confusion in the Plymouth box, Mason-Clark at first failing to divert the ball goalwards. But Torp was alert to the ball dropping at the back post and squared to provide Mason-Clark the simplest of finishes, the forward poking in from inside the six-yard box.

Lampard made a triple sub himself, Sidiki Cherif replacing Awoniyi for his debut, while Josh Eccles and Brandon Thomas-Asante also entered. Joe Edwards, the Plymouth midfielder, arrived from the bench but his first notable action was to inadvertently swipe at Thomas-Asante in the box when trying to clear the leftovers of a Coventry corner, giving the referee, Elliott Swallow, no choice but to award a penalty. Torp capped the scoring, thrashing the spot-kick into the top corner.

Sports.title: Manchester United confirm Carlos Baleba signing as midfield spend nears £150m
Sports.content:
Manchester United have completed the signing of the Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m. The Cameroon international is the third midfielder to join this summer, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba has signed a five-year contract with the option to extend for 12 months after United agreed a £65m deal plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on with Brighton. It takes the club’s spend on midfielders to about £148m.

Santos and Tielemans have arrived from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively during a summer when Casemiro left and Manuel Ugarte sustained a serious knee injury.

“It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams,” Baleba said. “Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”

United made a move to bring in Baleba last summer but cooled their pursuit when Brighton made it clear he was not leaving. Baleba was not at his best last season but that did not put off United, who stepped up their interest in the 22-year-old a week ago.

United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, said: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

“We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.”

Sports.title: Delap heads to Forest for £50m as Chelsea open talks to sell Jackson to Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a deal worth £50m to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, who have also opened talks over selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.

Xabi Alonso has made João Pedro and Danny Welbeck his main strikers this season, leaving his other frontmen to seek opportunities elsewhere.

Forest were one of several clubs interested in Delap, who has struggled since joining Chelsea from Ipswich for £30m last summer, and will pay a club record of £45m plus £5m in add-ons for the 23-year-old.

Delap managed only one league goal last season and was hindered by injuries after leaving Ipswich. But the former Manchester City striker was a key target for Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, and has a chance to revive his career at the City Ground.

Chelsea are focused on outgoings before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday and are also hoping to sell Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich last season. The Senegal international is valued at £65m and has been earmarked by Villa as a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.

Chelsea are not willing to agree to another loan for Jackson and want his valuation met but Villa are likely to press for a favourable payment schedule to ensure they can afford a permanent deal. Atlético Madrid are also interested in the 25-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Villarreal in 2023. Unai Emery, Villa’s manager, worked with Jackson at Villarreal.

West Ham’s clear out after relegation from the Premier League is expected to continue with El Hadji Malick Diouf joining Brentford for about £35m. The clubs are in discussions over a deal for the left-back and an agreement is likely soon.

Diouf wants to leave and was left out of the squad when Nuno Espírito Santo’s side continued their disappointing start to the Championship season by losing 2-1 at home against Charlton last Saturday.

West Ham signed the Senegal international for £19m from Slavia Prague last year. Brentford have made four signings and are plan to strengthen further.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Nuno, who is understood to be under growing pressure after West Ham’s flat start, has had his hand weakened by a host of players hoping to force their way out. The Mexico midfielder Edson Álvarez has not been involved in the first two league games and is the subject of interest from Olympiakos and Real Sociedad.

Torino have had a bid rejected for the midfielder Soungoutou Magassa, who is on Crystal Palace’s shortlist. Marseille could sign the French centre-back Jean-Clair Todibo. West Ham have raised funds through the sales of Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts, and have loaned Aaron Wan-Bissaka to Aston Villa and Niclas Füllkrug to Werder Bremen.

Sports.title: WSL academy teams to play in third tier after FA approves controversial plan
Sports.content:
Four Women’s Super League ­academy sides will play in the third tier of the ­pyramid from the ­2027-28 ­season after the ­controversial ­proposal was approved by the ­Football ­Association’s board.

The change forms part of what the FA described as a package of reforms to the Women’s National League “designed to strengthen the women’s football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players”.

Data showed that young English players were getting significantly fewer competitive ­minutes than their counterparts across Europe’s leading leagues, the FA said.

Quick Guide How do I 

WNL clubs will receive central funding for the first time and changes to the loan market will encourage clubs from the top two divisions to loan players to clubs in the third and fourth tiers.

The WSL academy teams will not be eligible for promotion and will be chosen against criteria to be ­developed in the coming months, the FA said. With the third tier split into two geographical regions, it is expected that two academies will be placed in the northern division and two in the southern.

Sue Day, director of women’s ­football at the FA, said:

“For the game to continue moving forward, the FA Women’s National League must evolve alongside the professional game, and we need to create more opportunities for talented young English players to develop in senior football.”

Sports.title: Xavi hopes time at the ‘university of football’ will end with Dutch success
Sports.content:
“My feeling today is that I’m going to the university of football.” Those were Xavi Hernández’s opening words at his presentation as the Netherlands coach on Tuesday. “I learned a lot from this university of football during my career as a player and as a coach. I have many connections with this country.”

Those connections date back to when Xavi was drafted as a youngster into La Masia, the famed Barcelona academy whose fundamentals are rooted in Dutch total football, inspired by Rinus Michels and Johan Cruyff. Xavi’s first-team debut came under Louis van Gaal, and he spent many years under Frank Rijkaard before becoming one of the main pillars of the dream team under Pep Guardiola, who was hugely inspired by Cruyff.

Xavi opened a Cruyff court – a multifunctional sport space for children – with Cruyff in his home town of Terrassa in 2014, and on Tuesday shared special memories of his time with Cruyff, who died in 2016. “With Johan in the last period of his life I had some meetings,” he said. “And he was always positive. Even when he was sick, he was positive. This is what I learned: always smiling. This is what I want to show here to the players. My first goal is to help them, and then enjoy the process. And we will be in a process to win.”

Xavi says he wants to “dominate the game, to take the initiative with the ball and at the same time our goal is to show everybody a team with passion, with desire and ambition. And this is very important for me as a coach.”

In the Netherlands, there has always been a strong emphasis on attacking football, which is why Xavi fitted the bill. The Catalan was asked whether he would use five defenders, as Van Gaal and Ronald Koeman did at times in recent years. “That this is not my idea,” he said. “We want to play in another system [like] 4-3-3, 4-2-3-1, 3-4-3. In those systems we can dominate the game more.”

Xavi said he had spoken to Frenkie de Jong – whom he coached at Barcelona – and Virgil van Dijk. He added that he would speak again to Van Dijk, the captain, in the near future to hear his ambitions with the team.

The 46-year-old was also clear he is willing to select players from the Saudi Pro League, something more relevant after Tijjani Reijnders moved from Manchester City to Al-Qadsiah last week. Two years ago, Koeman was clear when Steven Bergwijn moved to Al-Ittihad that the forward would no longer be selected because the league did not match the level he expected from his players.

View image in fullscreen Xavi Hernández said he wants to play attacking systems with the Netherlands to ‘dominate the game more’. Photograph: Stefan Koops/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock

“It’s a good league as well,” Xavi said. “Maybe we choose some players from Saudi, from Eredivisie, Premier League, La Liga. I don’t care about the leagues, I care about the performances and the players.”

Nigel de Jong, the director of elite football at the Dutch football federation (KNVB), had earlier been open about the process that led to Xavi’s appointment. He said he had first tested the waters with Guardiola, who indicated he did not want to take a job in the near future, before holding two meetings with Arne Slot, who eventually chose to remain a club coach.

De Jong then invited Xavi to Amsterdam for a meeting also attended by Clarence Seedorf, a member of the KNVB’s supervisory board. The following day De Jong and Seedorf spoke at length with Michael Reiziger, the Netherlands’ under-21s coach, who played alongside Xavi at Barcelona for several years.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

They were considering promoting Reiziger in a way similar to Luis de la Fuente’s journey with Spain, his knowledge of the country’s upcoming talents regarded as a major plus. When the meeting with Reiziger became known in the Dutch media, there was an assumption the former full-back would become the national team coach. But then, on 12 August, the KNVB announced Xavi, a decision that seemingly came out of the blue.

Xavi said drily that he was fine with the process. “Well, it’s not a bad position, after Guardiola and after Slot, no? At least you are at the podium. I don’t care if I’m the third [choice] or I’m the 10th. It’s a big honour to be here. He [De Jong] explained to me, very honestly: ‘We need your philosophy, we need to change with ambition, with passion.’ And we will work in this way.”

First up for Xavi is a Nations League game against Germany in Amsterdam on 24 September, when he will face Jürgen Klopp, who is also starting a new job. “I feel excited, I feel motivated,” Xavi said, “because we are playing against Germany, one of the best teams in Europe, one of the best coaches in recent years.”

Xavi, speaking in front of his staff, including Ruud van Nistelrooy, wants his team to adopt the Dutch style he saw as a young boy. “I remember when I was a kid, watching the Netherlands and watching good football,” he said, “and this is my way, this is my target.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s box office’: Gary Lineker admits wanting Roy Keane to join The Rest Is Football
Sports.content:
With an all-conquering podcast empire and a new deal that will make his football punditry show a regular fixture on Netflix, there seems little left for Gary Lineker to wish for.

However, while the former Match of the Day presenter is full of praise for Alan Shearer and Micah Richards – the fellow pundits on his The Rest Is Football show – Lineker has admitted to admiring a combative figure playing for his main rivals.

Asked which of the plethora of football pundits he would want to poach, Lineker admitted that Roy Keane’s brutal delivery and viral rants meant the former Manchester United captain would be his dream signing.

“He’s box office,” Lineker said during an appearance at the Edinburgh TV festival, before joking that, analytically, the Irishman “doesn’t give you that much”.

“He’s bloody good at being Roy Keane,” he said. “I’ve met Roy a few times. He’s really sweet … he just plays a character and he’s good at it. He’s really good at it, and he obviously knows his [stuff]. I was kidding about the analytical thing, a little bit.”

Keane is a member of a podcast team that has emerged as Lineker’s main opposition – Gary Neville’s The Overlap operation, which includes the Stick to Football show. Soon after The Rest Is Football signed up with Netflix, Stick to Football announced a similar deal with Disney.

While the rivalry is good natured, a tongue-in-cheek Lineker couldn’t help but add a slice of football needle, saying Keane “probably would” 

“You’ve got Gary [Neville] and his team, you’ve got Piers Morgan and his team [making the World Cup Uncensored] show, and they’re just trying to copy,” Lineker joked. “They’re trailing in our wake and I wish them all the very best. There is room, particularly in football. There’s a lot of competition.”

The deals bringing football podcasts to the world’s biggest streaming services are a sign of a thirst for sport content. Given the huge expense of live sporting rights, punditry has become a popular option.

The Rest is Football appeared in Netflix’s daily top 10 charts on every day of its 40-day run of daily episodes filmed during the World Cup, and the US company has opted to continue their partnership during the domestic season.

The Rest is Football obtained more than 7m monthly streams for its content alone last season, leading Lineker to joke that Neville’s outfit was “languishing miles behind”.

Lineker was interviewed on stage about his transition from footballer to presenter to media mogul, as the co-founder of successful podcast stable, Goalhanger. During the appearance, he explained why he continued to speak out on political issues, particularly Gaza.

In the last week, the Telegraph criticised him for reposting a video of Tony Greenstein, an anti-Zionist who was cleared last week of inviting support for Hamas. In the video, the activist said: “Zionism is in the tradition of the Nazis who persecuted Jews.”

11:01 Gary Lineker calls for Burnham to introduce wealth tax - The Latest

Lineker said: “I don’t think I speak much about politics, although politics is involved in everything that I speak about.

“I think ultimately you need to live with yourself and if I see things that upset me in humanitarian terms, then I find it quite upsetting, and it triggers me to use a platform that I would never have had before … People can disagree and that’s absolutely fine.”

Sports.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip‑drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go. Everything dies, baby, that’s a fact. But four‑part Amazon Prime documentaries make angels of us all.

So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

And this has been a genuine era, 10 years in the game and an entire tactical culture shift in the making. Unsurprisingly, there was an odd sense of lightness across those nine fixtures on Friday through to Sunday, of old bonds cast aside, even a little giddiness. Suddenly dad isn’t home. The chair by the door is empty. Let’s all just rip it up a bit, shall we?

This relies on a slightly out‑of‑date notion of what Guardiola‑ism became in its later years. But the fact is, something interesting did happen in those Friday‑to‑Sunday games. Think of pure Pep-ball and what are you seeing? Possession. Cold, high‑craft control. This is a coach who famously said: “My desire is to have 100% possession,” after a 5-1 thrashing of Arsenal in Munich during which Thiago Alcântara complete 122 passes.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledges the fans before City’s opener against Bournemouth. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Admittedly, Guardiola was speaking out of frustration that day, talking more about not losing the ball at key moments, possession as defence. But these ideas did have a profound mimetic effect in England. During Guardiola’s decade at Manchester City the team that had the least possession in the Premier League would win, on average, only 30%-35% of games, a figure that fell as low as 28% in 2021‑22 but which had begun to pick up in the last two seasons as even City’s own version of Pep‑ball became more mixed and next‑gen.

But this weekend the opposite thing happened. In six of nine games played from Friday to Sunday one team took significantly more possession while failing to win. Liverpool had 60% possession plus 27 shots but still just scrambled a draw and looked, frankly, pretty wild. Manchester United had 71% possession and were well beaten by Hull. Tottenham had 60 % possession and lost 3-0. Nottingham Forest had 56% and lost. Sunderland had 62%, Crystal Palace 58%, and both lost.

There were three exceptions to this, all outliers in their own way. Manchester City had 66% possession and won at home against Bournemouth, but spent 84 minutes looking like they were losing. Brighton had 73% possession and beat an Aston Villa team that had made a collective decision to play with their eyes closed and their legs on the wrong way round. Arsenal dominated every metric against a promoted Coventry team that looked, frankly, a little spooked by their first sight of that fresh Everest.

So, a tiny sample size. It may mean absolutely nothing. It could get flipped on its head before we hit September. Also, it is important to note that pure possession stats have rarely dictated with any certainty who will win a game. The top teams always tend to have most of the ball, thus skewing the overall stats.

Otherwise, possession has been a far less reliable guide to victory than, say, expected goals, which speaks clearly to the effectiveness of a system. Whereas simply keeping the ball is often a sign of the opposite of good health, of football as a collective anxiety attack, out there playing with your worry beads, tramping a horseshoe shape into the grass while your opponents mass for the decisive blitzkrieg.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But it wasn’t just the possession numbers that were notable this weekend. The rhythms of the matches were striking. All three Sunday games featured nine or 10 substitutes in the last 40 minutes or so, and a sense of two separate halves, of finishers brought into play, of a broken, episodic tactical to‑and‑fro in response to shifts in the scoreline and the flow. The World Cup also had that pattern. Maybe this is what football is now.

Mainly there was a striking level of targeted physicality, rehearsed blitz-transitions, groups of players running suddenly forward quickly in formation at certain triggering events. Anthony Elanga’s opener for Newcastle captured this best: 12 seconds, two passes, 70 metres covered in a single perfectly straight line, no off‑the‑cuff inventions or what you might call conventional “creativity”, but a perfect moment of planned collective intelligence and breathtaking athleticism.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This was the pattern elsewhere too, games defined by rapid breaks, by powerful players sourced for their ability to win duels and to carry the ball, and a weekend that felt like another ratcheting up in the Premier League’s journey into hyper‑physicality.

Isn’t it a trend? Is this the next stage in the league’s narrow but furiously intense evolution? There are several managers in new jobs who have reputations for the game of sprints, blitz‑ball: most notably Matthias Jaissle at Newcastle and Roberto De Zerbi at what was, on Saturday, the least De Zerbi‑ish of Spurs, a Spurs that seemed to have absorbed only the mouse part – play dead, hide, roll over – of that fast‑breaking cat‑and‑mouse football.

There are two things worth saying about this. This is not a rejection of Guardiolaism and positional play. Keeping the ball was always about preparing for the moments when you don’t have it. Guardiola’s later Manchester City team would often win by direct means.

But pure possession can also be boringly risk-averse, a kind of footballing atrophy where everyone just sits quivering on the touchline like a swarm of beached jellyfish at dusk. The spectacle is more gripping when the emphasis is on those transitions either side of the passing patterns.

More specifically, it is also an interesting development for Pep’s successor at City, Enzo Maresca, Coolio to his Tupac, whose methods are still very much pure Pep origins, based in control of the ball and rigid positionism, like the last soldier still fighting the second world war from inside a bush on Iwo Jima in 1976.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga celebrates his superb strike against Liverpool. Photograph: Simon Davies/ProSports/Shutterstock

Is Maresca ready for this? Is he even ahead of it? He gave a televised interview at the weekend where he spoke about the tension between control and risk, possession and creativity, and where he defined players being encouraged to run into unexpected positions as “chaos”. On Monday morning there were headlines describing the Premier League weekend in those terms. But this isn’t chaos. We’ve seen chaos. We’ve seen attack ships on fire off the shoulder of Orion, jinking wingers, dogs of war, hitting the space, Lee Chapman, Rod Wallace and Eric Cantona making heavy metal music with two bass guitars and an antique viola. You want chaos. We can give you chaos.

What the Premier League brought at the weekend, the quick breaks, the freedom to attack at selected moments, was more a kind of hyper-managed shock and awe, targeted speed and physicality born out of calculated risk, numbers, data, heavy briefings.

It was also exciting to watch, which is no bad thing in the world’s most tightly contested, space‑averse league. No doubt there will be tightening, a reaction to the reaction, instant counter‑moves and contingency planning. August can also be odd and silly season-ish, the dog days of a World Cup summer. But it did at times feel as if we were in a post‑something moment. If not quite post‑Pep, whose influence will continue to loom, a tactical Machiavelli with plenty of tapes still left in the vault.

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.

“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling is charged with dangerous driving and possessing 'hippy crack' after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after his £270,000 Lamborghini crashed in May, it has been reported.

The former Premier League star, 31, who was arrested at the scene of the collision, faces two years in prison if convicted of the charges.

Police were called to the M3 in Hampshire on May 28 to reports of a Lamborghini swerving around the road just before 9am.

Footage obtained by the Daily Mail showed the black luxury 4x4 veering across the three carriageways as other vehicles dodged out of the way.

The driver appeared to be inhaling from a balloon - which is how people ingest laughing gas, also known as 'hippy crack'.

Minutes later, Sterling allegedly crashed the vehicle into the motorway barriers and was cuffed by Hampshire Police.

The force said he would not give a sample after his arrest - leading to a third charge of failing to to supply a specimen.

A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman told The Sun: 'Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

Raheem Sterling has reportedly been charged with dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide, and failing to supply a specimen

Footage obtained by the Daily Mail showed Starling's black Lamborghini M-way scraping the motorway central reservation, minutes before it crashed

The driver appeared to be inhaling from a balloon, just visible as a dark circle above

'The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.'

They added that Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates Court on September 15.

The charges mark a new low for Sterling, who left Chelsea in January after being dropped from their line-up and not playing since May 2024.

In February he joined Dutch club Feyenoord Rotterdam, but that deal ended in summer and he has been without a club since - despite wanting to play.

The motorist who provided the dashcam footage of Sterling's sports car swerving told the Mail: 'I was in the middle lane and without warning a black Lamborghini pulled in front of me, forcing me to slow.

'I dropped back. I'm a driving instructor after all.

'The car turned back into the inside lane but the driver put his foot down and veered right across all three lanes and seemed to just avoid hitting the central reservation.

'It's a powerful car and he could have easily gone through the central reservation if he'd hit the accelerator.

'A van driver behind him was forced to brake and he then shot off again and turned back across three lanes again into the inside lane.

Sterling is engaged to long-term girlfriend Paige Milian (pictured)

Sterling, here playing for Feyenoord in February, has been without a team since the summer

'This was all caught on dashcam from 8.45am on Thursday. It was just before Junction 4a southbound on the M3.

'The motorist was all over the place but I had no idea it was Raheem Sterling until I saw that he'd been arrested on suspicion of drug-driving by the Minley Interchange.

'I like Raheem but as a driving instructor I'm very concerned.

'He could have easily caused himself - and others - a great deal of harm. He was very fortunate that he did not do so.'

Sterling's representatives declined to comment when contacted by the Daily Mail after the crash, but a source close to the player explained how he had had a hellish two years.

The source said: 'The psychological strain that has been put on him is immeasurable. Isolated. The second he touches a ball, being told he's a flop and he's finished. Mocked. Heckled.

'He moved to the Netherlands to escape and rediscover his love for the game but the negativity followed. It's been an extremely tough couple of years for him and this incident encompasses that.'

Sterling started his career at QPR but broke through at Liverpool as a teenager, before leaving Anfield for Manchester City in 2015, where he won ten major trophies, including the Premier League four times.

He played 82 times for the England senior team, with his last appearance in the 2-1 defeat by France in the quarter-finals of the 2022 World Cup.

However, since leaving City for Chelsea in a £50million deal in 2022 he has endured a torrid spell, which saw him exiled at Stamford Bridge before a failed loan spell with Arsenal and a move to Dutch giants Feyenoord, where he made just eight appearances with no goals.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes crowned PFA Player of the Year after record-breaking season for Man United... and he's one of just TWO stars outside Arsenal and Man City in the Team of the Year
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has been named the PFA Players' Player of the Year after a landmark 2025-26 campaign in which the Manchester United captain broke the Premier League record for most assists in a single season.

Fernandes surpassed the previous mark of 20, jointly held by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne, on the final day of the season when he set up Patrick Dorgu's header against Brighton to register his 21st assist of the campaign.

Fernandes has already won the Premier League Player of the Season and the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year accolades, and completed the hat-trick by collecting the prestigious, player-voted award at Manchester's Opera House on Tuesday evening.

He was United's first to claim the PFA Players' Player of the Year since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

The Portugal midfielder was the sole United player to have been named in the PFA's Premier League Team of the Year, and he is joined by Brentford's Igor Thiago as the only other non-Manchester City or Arsenal player in the side.

David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice all made up a heavily defensive Arsenal contingent, while Nico O'Reilly, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo and Erling Haaland completed City's representation.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was crowned PFA Player of the Year on Tuesday

Fernandes, who attended with his wife Ana, was also named in the PFA Team of the Year

Fernandes had already won the Premier League Player of the Season and the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year accolades, and completed the hat-trick on Tuesday evening

Mohamed Salah was named PFA Players' Player of the Year last year, but no Liverpool players made the cut this time.

O'Reilly also scooped the Men's Young Player of the Year award, beating team-mate Cherki as well as Max Dowman, Junior Kroupi, Kobbie Mainoo and Rio Ngumoha to the prize.

Elsewhere, Everton's Hayden Hackney was named the Championship Player of the Year after playing a key role in Middlesbrough's run to the play-off final in May. He signed for David Moyes' side in July after missing out on promotion with his boyhood club.

Dom Ballard took home the League One title after a standout season for Leyton Orient while Swindon's Aaron Drinan won the League Two award.

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw lifted the Women's Players' Player of the Year award for the second time after also collecting it in 2024, becoming only the third player to win it twice after Lucy Bronze (2014 and 2017) and Fran Kirby (2018 and 2021).

Shaw was the WSL's Golden Boot winner last season, scoring 21 goals in 22 matches as she helped fire her team to the top-flight trophy for the first time in 10 years.

The other nominees for the top prize in the women's game were Manchester City team-mate Yui Hasegawa, Chelsea's Lauren James, Manchester United's Jess Park, Arsenal's Alessia Russo and Aston Villa's Kirsty Hanson.

Nico O'Reilly (left) won the PFA Young Player, while Declan Rice was in the Team of the Year

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw lifted the Women's Players' Player of the Year award

Arsenal's Olivia Smith scooped the Young Player of the Year award after a fine season

PREMIER LEAGUE AND WSL TEAMS OF THE YEAR Premier League team of the year: David Raya (Arsenal); Jurrien Timber (Arsenal), William Saliba (Arsenal), Gabriel Magalhaes (Arsenal), Nico O'Reilly (Man City); Bruno Fernandes (Man United), Declan Rice (Arsenal), Rayan Cherki (Man City); Erling Haaland (Man City), Antoine Semenyo (Man City), Igor Thiago (Brentford). WSL team of the year: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea); Kerstin Casparij (Man City), Toko Koga (Tottenham), Ellie Carpenter (Chelsea), Emily Fox (Arsenal); Yui Hasegawa (Man City), Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal), Jess Park (Man United); Bunny Shaw (Man City), Alessia Russo (Arsenal), Lauren James (Chelsea).

Hannah Hampton, Kerstin Casparij, Toko Koga, Ellie Carpenter and Emily Fox made up the remainder of the PFA WSL Team of the Year.

Arsenal's Olivia Smith, the former most expensive transfer in women's history, scooped the Young Player of the Year award.

The 22-year-old Canada international became the first women's player to surpass the seven-figure barrier last summer when Arsenal signed her from Liverpool for £1 million, and had an impressive campaign, scoring five goals and recording three assists.

Sports.title: Man United youngster Chido Obi Martin linked with loan move to Europe, Red Devils land Carlos Baleba while Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man United youngster Chido Obi Martin linked with loan move to Europe, Red Devils land Carlos Baleba while Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap deal: WINDOW WATCH

To catch up on all of yesterday's developments - including Aston Villa making contact with AC Milan over Rafael Leao - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

United youngster linked with Feyenoord

Manchester United forward Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Feyenoord.

The Dutch side, coached by Giovanni van Bronckhorst, want cover in case they lose a forward in the final stages of the window.

Obi Martin, a Denmark U21 international, had interest from Cologne earlier in the window.

Feyenoord would also offer Champions League football.

Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Dutch side Feyenoord

Forest close in on Delap deal

Nottingham Forest and Chelsea are closing on a £45million deal for Liam Delap.

Talks intensified on Monday following Chelsea's game at Fulham and a verbal agreement is in place for the 23-year-old to link up with Oliver Glasner's team.

He is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours.

Liam Delap is expected to undergo a Nottingham Forest medical in the next 24 hours

United complete Baleba deal

Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal.

‘I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level,' said the 22-year-old, who has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford.

‘The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.’

For more on this story click HERE

Carlos Baleba with Manchester United's director of football Jason Wilcox

Gonzalez says goodbye to City ahead of £50m Newcastle move

Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez is travelling to the North East to finalise his £50m move to Newcastle United.

The 24-year-old Spaniard will undergo his medical in the next 24 hours.

Gonzalez said his farewells to City team-mates this morning and the deal is set to be £47m plus £3m in add-ons.

Nico Gonzalez will become Newcastle United's latest signing of the summer

City defender Kabore set for Wrexham medical

Manchester City defender Issa Kabore is due for a medical at Wrexham after they agreed a £2million fee. The 25-year-old spent last season on loan at Wrexham and wants to continue with the club as they attempt to take the next step up to the Premier League.

Kabore, who has 55 caps for Burkina Faso, has had eight loan spells since joining City from Mechelen in 2020.

Ipswich Town want £9m for Wrexham target Anis Mehmeti and Birmingham City are also interested.

Issa Kabore, pictured while on loan at Luton in 2024, is set to move to Wrexham

Bees still buzzing about Diouf

Brentford are continuing discussions with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf. The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season.

West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf is a target for Brentford

Forest talk over £13.6m move for Andre

Nottingham Forest are in talks over a £13.6million move for Corinthians midfielder Andre.

The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but has quickly established himself as one of the best young midfield talents in the Brazilian league.

AC Milan attempted to sign him in January but he wanted to see out the season with Corinthians. Crystal Palace have also been watching him .

Forest have been looking to strengthen their midfield since selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City.

They have made offers for Lucas Bergvall at Spurs and Tijjani Reijnders who left City for Al Qadsiah.

Villa enquire over Kofane

Aston Villa have made an enquiry to Bayer Leverkusen for striker Christian Kofane.

As well as working on Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson, Villa want another forward.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed, they were rebuffed in an enquiry for Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta but have now turned to Kofane.

The 20-year-old's agent was in England earlier this summer talking to the likes of Everton and Arsenal.

However, at this stage Leverkusen do not wish to sell.

Wrexham close on £8m move

Wrexham are closing in on a move for highly-rated Angers wing-back Jacques Ekomie as they look to bolster their side for a Premier League push.

Phil Parkinson has been keen to add to his squad before next week’s deadline and it’s understood there has been a breakthrough with Angers for Ekomie, who is valued at around £8million.

Co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac were in attendance for Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Watford and Parkinson revealed he had a ‘good chat’ with the Hollywood pair about transfers.

Ekomie has been a man in demand this summer with interest from Hamburg and West Ham but Wrexham are confident they have won the race to land the 23-year-old.

Wrexham's first bid for Ekomie, rejected on Friday, was £4.3m.

They are also trying for Millwall forward Femi Azeez and Ipswich's attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti.

NATHAN SALT

Olympiacos in for Edson

Olympiacos have made an offer to take West Ham defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez on loan.

The Mexico international has also had interest from Real Sociedad and Ajax so far.

Doncaster living the life O'Reilly

Doncaster Rovers are set to sign Aston Villa starlet Tommi O’Reilly on a season-long loan.

A plethora of clubs, including Sheffield Wednesday, have been interested in the midfielder who got over 20 goal contributions in League Two last season while on loan at Crewe.

Tommi O'Reilly starred at Crewe Alexandra on loan last season

Tottenham seal Savinho deal

Tottenham have confirmed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that a fee had been agreed comprising £75m plus £10m in add-ons.

Roberto De Zerbi's side lost 3-0 at Brentford in their Premier League opener and their new signing will come into the mix ahead of tomorrow's League Cup clash with Charlton. Spurs are also expected to bring in Omar Marmoush in a double swoop from City.

Savinho said: 'It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here. It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.

'As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.'

De Zerbi described Savinho as 'a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity.

'We’re very pleased to have him with us, and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.'

Savinho signs on the dotted line for his move to Spurs

Pinnock in for Coventry medical

Ethan Pinnock is due to have his medical at Coventry today ahead of singing a three-year contract with an option to extend.

The promoted club agreed a £6m fee with Brentford for the 33-year-old defender yesterday.

Ethan Pinnock is set to bolster Frank Lampard's squad at Coventry

Chelsea in talks over Guiu exit

Napoli are continuing talks with Chelsea for Marc Guiu and defender Mamadou Sarr’s proposed loan to Sociedad is progressing. Chelsea have asked about Atalanta defensive prospect Honest Anahor.

Villa look at Leao deal

Aston Villa are exploring the finances of a deal for AC Milan's Rafael Leao.

Daily Mail Sport reported last night that the club had made contact over the winger, 27. Turkish giants Galatasaray remain in the mix for the Portuguese as well.

Rafael Leao in pre-season action against Chelsea

Bakwa off to Lille

Nottingham Forest winger Dilane Bakwa is joining Lille on loan.

The 23-year-old signed for Forest from Strasbourg last September in a deal worth £30million but has failed to have the desired impact.

He is due for a medical today and will play in the Champions League with Lille.

Dilane Bakwa is set to leave after just one season at the City Ground

City set to go back to Enzo

Manchester City are expected to go back in for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

The Blues previously set City a deadline of 5pm on August 13 to pay £120m to get the deal done - a deadline City did not meet.

But contact has continued with his agent Javier Pastore so City know the 25-year-old is open to coming and now they are set to come back in for the midfielder, who played the final half-hour of Chelsea's 3-2 win away at Fulham on Monday night.

Sports.title: Serena Williams makes spectacular return to US Open as she teams up with Carlos Alcaraz in mixed power pairing... four years after stepping back from tennis at the Grand Slam
Sports.content:
Serena Williams makes spectacular return to US Open as she teams up with Carlos Alcaraz in mixed power pairing... four years after stepping back from tennis at the Grand Slam

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Serena Williams made an emotional return to Flushing Meadows on Tuesday when she teamed up with Spanish sensation Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open's mixed doubles event.

The tennis icon, 44, continued her comeback tour, returning to the Grand Slam where she bowed out of the sport four years ago.

Williams announced that she would be 'evolving away' from tennis following the 2022 US Open. But, after returning to tennis's major stages at Wimbledon and the Cincinnati Open earlier this year, she stepped into the spotlight on Arthur Ashe once again.

The US Tennis Association announced on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz, 23, had been handed a wild card for the year's final Grand Slam.

The pair were granted entry into the star-studded 16-team field competing for a $1million prize, sealing a stunning return to the US Open for Williams.

They took to the iconic Arthur Ashe court on Tuesday afternoon, facing Lloyd Glasspool and Erin Routliffe in the first round of the event.

Serena Williams made an emotional return to the US Open in the mixed doubles on Tuesday

The 44-year-old teamed up with Spanish ace Carlos Alcaraz (pictured) in the event

The tennis legend stepped back from the sport following the 2022 US Open

It will be the 44-year-old's first time playing at the US Open since 2022. The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion returned to tennis earlier this summer.

But she is not planning to play singles in New York. The USTA had been holding one women's wild card - presumably in case Williams wanted it. On Saturday, however, organizers announced it had gone to American Sofia Kenin , the 2020 Australian Open champion.

Williams played singles at Wimbledon, losing in the first round and sustaining a knee injury, before teaming up with older sister Venus to play doubles at the Cincinnati Open. In their first match together since the 2022 US Open, the sisters were beaten by Peyton Stearns and Marta Kostyuk, 6-2, 1-6, 10-8.

Serena Williams has won a US Open mixed doubles title before, taking the crown in 1998 alongside Max Mirnyi, who now works with Aryna Sabalenka . Nearly three decades on, the competition is now a star-studded, two-day competition, with Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic among the other big names taking part this year.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, announced this week he would return to defend his US Open singles title after being sidelined since April with a right wrist injury.

News of his comeback - and his partnership with Williams - is a huge boost for fans after rival Jannik Sinner pulled out.

The world No 1 announced on Friday that he will miss the US Open with a knee injury.

In a statement on social media, the Italian wrote: 'Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year.

Serena Williams was world No.1 in singles the day Carlos Alcaraz was born.



23 years later, the two join forces in Grand Slam mixed doubles! pic.twitter.com/MvUSxZXlyf — US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 25, 2026

The tennis icon continued her comeback tour, returning to the Grand Slam in New York

Serena Williams' Wimbledon singles comeback came to an early end on Tuesday

The legend was supported by her husband Alexis Ohanian and their two daughters

'We have been back on court in Monte Carlo over the last couple of days and have realised that I still need more time to recover from my right knee issue.

'I'm obviously very sad and disappointed, as New York has a special place in my heart. I was very much looking forward to coming back and playing in the electric atmosphere in front of the great fans there.'

Sinner turned pro in 2018 and has never missed a Grand Slam tournament in his entire career, winning five in total - including the US Open two years ago and Wimbledon this summer.

The 25-year-old has been dominant so far in 2026, winning the first five ATP Masters 1000 events, two of which in the US in Indian Wells and Miami.

After crashing out of Wimbledon in the first round and suffering a similar fate alongside sister Venus in the women's doubles in Cincinnati, many have questioned if Williams still possesses her titan talent.

Others may be more focused on the question mark over one particular detail of her preparation -whether Williams has continued to use GLP-1 jabs managed by telehealth company Ro, of which she became a vocal paid spokesperson for last year.

Williams returned to tennis this summer and played with sister Venus at the Cincinnati Open

The seven-time Wimbledon champion's husband Alexis Ohanian sits on the company's board and was an early investor. As recently as this February Williams, the company's celebrity face, featured in a Super Bowl advert for the brand and its Zepbound tirzepatide jab, which is also marketed under the name Mounjaro.

Williams, who is said to have lost close to two and a half stone, or 34 pounds (15kg) using the drug, previously called her challenge to lose weight following the birth of her two children 'the one opponent (she) couldn't beat'.

It remains unclear as to whether Williams has continued to use the drug, which also treats symptoms of diabetes, with her publicist declining to comment when asked by the Atlantic.

But although GLP-1s are not banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), they are one of the drugs under ongoing investigation as to whether they might be classed as performance-enhancing in the future.

Sports.title: Chelsea's summer clear-out continues as Blues close in on agreeing staggering £115MILLION double sale of strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson
Sports.content:
Chelsea's summer clear-out continues as Blues close in on agreeing staggering £115MILLION double sale of strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have agreed a staggering £50million sale Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest.

Delap is now in line to leave Stamford Bridge after only a single season, with the Blues having triggered his £30m release clause at Ipswich Town last summer.

He scored one Premier League goal in 28 games in 2025-26, and two in 41 in all competitions.

Delap was missing from the Chelsea squad which defeated Fulham 3-2 in their first Premier League fixture of the season.

The 23-year-old had been training separately to Xabi Alonso’s main group at their Cobham base after being made available for sale, along with Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson is also closing in on a £65m switch to Aston Villa. That would see Chelsea secure their asking price for the 25-year-old Senegalese.

Chelsea have agreed a £50million fee with Nottingham Forest to sell them Liam Delap

Nicolas Jackson is also nearing a £65million move to Aston Villa from Chelsea

The Chelsea star is understood to be keen on a reunion with former boss Unai Emery

They had been seeking at least £50m for Delap. It is believed Forest’s agreement involves £45m plus £5m in add-ons.

It represents a remarkable profit secured by Chelsea after a disappointing campaign for Delap, whose No 9 shirt was handed to Joao Pedro before this current season started.

Delap had been keen to stay at Chelsea and prove himself, but he became surplus this summer.

With Joao Pedro untouchable at the front of Chelsea's attack, they also signed Danny Welbeck from Brighton and have Emmanuel Emegha. Jackson and Marc Guiu are in line to leave.

Sports.title: Stars hit the red carpet at the PFA Awards: Bruno Fernandes is joined by WAG as Declan Rice leads FIVE Arsenal players in attendance with football world descending on Manchester for bash
Sports.content:
Stars hit the red carpet at the PFA Awards: Bruno Fernandes is joined by WAG as Declan Rice leads FIVE Arsenal players in attendance with football world descending on Manchester for bash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A plethora of key figures within English football have all descended upon Manchester ahead of Tuesday night's Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Awards.

The annual ceremony is taking place this year at the Opera House Theatre.

Among those in attendance sees representation from several Premier League teams.

Champions Arsenal are represented by a key quintet of David Raya, Jurrien Timber, Gabriel Magalhaes, William Saliba and Declan Rice. Those five will hope to be involved in at least the PFA Team of the Year, while potentially collecting the prize for PFA Player of the Year.

Arsenal were in a title pursuit with Manchester City all of last season and beat them in the Community Shield two Sundays ago.

That quintet will cross paths with City trio Antoine Semenyo, Rayan Cherki and Nico O'Reilly who are also there.

Arsenal stars David Raya, Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba (left to right) were on the red carpet ahead of the PFA Awards in Manchester on Tuesday night

Manchester City were represented at the bash by Antoine Semenyo (centre) and Rayan Cherki

Semenyo enjoyed a prolific season at Bournemouth and City last term, while O'Reilly had a breakout campaign which saw him end it as part of England head coach Thomas Tuchel's - who is also attending - World Cup squad which reached the semi-finals.

Aged just 21, the City academy graduate is the favourite to win PFA Young Player of the Year.

City's bitter rivals Manchester United are represented by head coach Michael Carrick, CEO Omar Berrada and Bruno Fernandes.

The pair have had a busy day following the £70million transfer completion of Carlos Baleba from Brighton and Hove Albion.

Baleba will add some much-needed dynamism to United's midfield and will play behind captain Fernandes - who is another leading contender for the PFA Player of the Year award after a fantastic 2025-26 where he broke the Premier League assists record for a single season with 21.

In May, he won the Football Writers' Association's men's Footballer of the Year award and was named Premier League player of the season, meaning it could be a clean sweep of accolades if he's victorious come 9pm.

Liverpool icon Kenny Dalglish also donned the red carpet alongside his wife Marina.

Arsenal are also well represented in the women's game in Manchester with Alessia Russo, Mariona Caldentey, Emily Fox and Olivia Smith representing the Gunners too.

Nico O'Reilly (left) could win PFA Young Player, in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel there

Bruno Fernandes registered a record-breaking 21 assists in the Premier League last season

Michael Carrick (left) and Omar Berrada are among those representing Manchester United

Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish smiles for the cameras alongside his wife Marina

Arsenal Women's Olivia Smith, Mariona Caldentey, Alessia Russo, and Emily Fox (left-right) attended Tuesday's event at the Manchester Opera Theatre

Former Lionesses Karen Carney, Eni Aluko, Jordan Nobbs and Toni Duggan are also in the crowd for Tuesday night's showpiece.

In terms of former male footballers the likes of Mikael Silvestre, Sebastian Bassong, Ashley Young, Asmir Begovic, Kolo Toure are also present.

Ex-Manchester United and Arsenal defender Silvestre hit the headlines on Monday after calling out FIFA president Gianni Infantino, telling him to stand down.

Silvestre, who is part of FIFA's Players' Voice Panel, took to X to demand change, writing: 'Enough is enough!'

The post, which went on to call for structural change within FIFA, was shared by France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit as well as Lioness Lucy Bronze.

Infantino is also facing calls to quit from his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in the wake of a hugely controversial plan to sell stakes in a company to run the World Cup to private investors.

And players have now begun to speak out against the 56-year-old, with Monday's widely shared statement evidential of those who 'share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world'.

Karen Carney (left) and Mikael Silvestre are among the ex-footballers at Tuesday's ceremony

It added: 'Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA's current leadership.

'For too long we've seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

'Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership's ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football.'

Silvestre's interjection is significant given it effectively comes from within the FIFA fold, with the Players' Voice Panel a 16-strong group formed by the global governing body to monitor and advise on initiatives to tackle racism.

The statement continued: 'Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.

'We call on all stakeholders to step forward and help reshape the future of our sport.'

Sports.title: Sir Billy Boston dead aged 92: Rugby league legend - and the sport's first knight - was a gentle giant and a breaker of barriers, writes OLIVER HOLT - he belongs in the same company as Jackie Robinson and Arthur Ashe
Sports.content:
Sir Billy Boston dead aged 92: Rugby league legend - and the sport's first knight - was a gentle giant and a breaker of barriers, writes OLIVER HOLT - he belongs in the same company as Jackie Robinson and Arthur Ashe

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Sir Billy Boston was a giant of a man, who spoke with gentleness and humility and self-deprecation and who bequeathed a gift to the sport of Rugby League that will last far beyond the records he set and the tries he scored and the entertainment he provided to millions as a player for Wigan.

Sir Billy, who died on Tuesday at the age of 92, was a breaker of barriers, a man who deserves to be remembered in the same company as heroes like Jackie Robinson, major league baseball’s first black player in the modern era, and Arthur Ashe, who swept away so many prejudices in the game of tennis.

Boston became the first non-white player to represent Great Britain on a Lions tour in 1954. He scored 36 tries in 18 appearances in Australia and New Zealand, and played in 31 international Test matches.

The numbers say that he scored 478 tries in 488 matches for Wigan and played in six Challenge Cup finals for the team but his standing in the game and in the world of sport as a whole, the way he carried himself, the way he wore his greatness lightly, made him a hero to many more.

‘Heartbroken to hear my friend Sir Billy Boston has died,’ prime minister Andy Burnham wrote yesterday. ‘Billy was one of the greatest Rugby League players of all time but also one of the kindest and most down-to-earth people you could ever wish to meet. He always had time for people and gave so much to back to his adopted home, Wigan…A giant of a man in every way.’

Today we mourn the loss of a true sporting icon, Sir Billy Boston, who has passed away surrounded by his family.



Rugby League’s first knight, a Wigan legend, and "Everybody's Hero," his legacy on and off the field will endure for eternity.



Rest in peace, Sir Billy. 🍒⚪️ pic.twitter.com/y8Dw9XPPGi — Wigan Warriors 🍒⚪️ (@WiganWarriorsRL) August 25, 2026

Sir Billy Boston was hailed as 'simply the greatest' by Wigan head coach Matt Peet

For the first 130 years of Rugby League’s existence, the establishment did not judge a single one of its players worthy of a knighthood and the omission felt like a sign of society’s disregard and disdain for the sport.

In the same period, rugby union was awarded 20 knighthoods, yachting 12, motor racing eight, horse racing eight and sheep shearing one. It had begun to feel as if rugby league was a pariah.

But two years ago, Billy Boston changed that. His stature was such that he had already had three statues in his honour - in Cardiff, where he was born, at Wembley, where he played in those Challenge Cup finals, and in Wigan, where he lived for the last 72 years of his life – and then there came the final symbolism of the knighthood.

I met him in a hotel on Piccadilly, in London, on the eve of the ceremony at Buckingham Palace in June 2025. He was accompanied to London by Wigan Warriors owner Mike Danson and club legend Kris Radlinski, now Wigan’s chief executive. Boston was 90 by then and a little frail but he still carried himself like a king of old.

Wigan have indicated that they will pay tribute to Boston ahead of their Betfred Super League match against Hull KR on Thursday night and that day in London, Danson and Radlinski both radiated pride in him.

They knew what a hero he was to so many. They knew what he meant to fans of the sport and beyond. They knew he was a crossover star. ‘We’ve just never had that breakthrough moment before,’ Radlinski said.

‘One of the problems is we promote humility and create these humble guys, but we actually need them to be superstars. One thing about rugby league in our town and many northern teams is everybody lives in the town and access is unbelievable. So it’s your biggest strength, but also your biggest weakness.’

Danson also pointed out that only a small percentage of knighthoods are earned by people from the north. If you are northern and working class, that percentage shrinks even more. Boston smashed through that barrier, as well. His death came only four days after the funeral of his wife, Lady Joan, to whom he had been married for 70 years.

Boston grew up playing rugby union before switching codes to sign for Wigan in 1953 at the age of 19 and graced the sport throughout the 50s and 60s. The Welsh Rugby Union paid tribute to him, too, yesterday, and Wigan head coach Matt Peel praised one of the town’s favourite sons.

Boston was knighted by the King last year

'Billy Boston is woven into the fabric of this club,’ Peel said. ‘Every day we walk through the doors, we’re reminded that we have a responsibility to represent all those who have gone before us and made Wigan Warriors what it is today. Billy stands at the very top of that history.

'Those fortunate enough to have seen him play tell me he was simply the greatest. His achievements, the man he was and the standards he set will continue to inspire everyone who pulls on this shirt.

'His legacy goes far beyond records and trophies. His impact on Wigan, on rugby league and on the wider sporting world was recognised at the very highest level. We will do everything we can to honour his memory by representing this club with the pride, humility and excellence that he embodied.

'Sir Billy Boston will always be one of Wigan Warriors’ greatest sons, and he will never be forgotten.'

Sports.title: Man United COMPLETE £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton - as Michael Carrick looks to bolster midfield after Hull horror show on Premier League opening day
Sports.content:
Man United COMPLETE £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton - as Michael Carrick looks to bolster midfield after Hull horror show on Premier League opening day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal.

Baleba has signed a five-year-contract at Old Trafford with the option to extend it by 12 months after agreeing personal terms and passing a medical.

United will pay an initial £65m and up to £5m more in add-ons to Brighton who have included a sell-on clause as part of the deal.

The 22-year-old Cameroon international, who is currently sidelined with an ankle injury, becomes United's third midfield signing of the summer after the club spent a total of £85m on Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba, who has been linked with United for more than a year, said: 'It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

'I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

Carlos Baleba has completed a £70million transfer to Manchester United from Brighton

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford, with the option for an extra year

'The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.'

United's director of football Jason Wilcox is delighted to complete the club's midfield rebuild after Casemiro left as a free agent and Manuel Ugarte was ruled out for much of this season with a knee ligament injury.

'Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further,' said Wilcox. 'He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

'We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

'Carlos' determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions.'

Fans will be relieved to see United get the deal over the line, particularly after their woeful start to the season at Hull City on Saturday.

First-half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy, both coming from set-pieces, left the Mancunians in the dust.

United's midfield of Santos and Tielemans with Fernandes ahead of them, lacked the dynamism that Baleba should hopefully aid with once he's fit.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez makes decision on transfer with Chelsea braced for £120m bid
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez makes decision on transfer with Chelsea braced for £120m bid

A deadline for interested clubs to meet Chelsea's demands for Enzo Fernandez passed a fortnight ago - but the Argentina midfielder still has his sights sets on a move to Manchester City

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez's future at Chelsea is still uncertain (Image: James Gill/Getty Images)

Enzo Fernandez is ready to make a £120m last-minute move to Manchester City.

‌



Chelsea are braced for City to make a bid for the Argentina midfielder in what will be their biggest deal of the summer. Fernandez, 25, is believed to be keen on moving to the Etihad which would mean a reunion with City boss Enzo Maresca.

‌



Chelsea will demand a profit on the £106m they paid for Fernandez in 2023 while they may also insist on getting a replacement lined up. They have been linked with Real Madrid midfielder Eduardo Camavinga and any deal for Fernandez would be complicated - but City are ready to make a push to make it happen.

‌



Chelsea set a strict deadline for clubs to meet their £120m price two weeks ago - and that has now passed.

But City are ready to make a formal bid to get the mega deal over the line before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday.

‌



Fernandez has been unsettled at Chelsea since being axed last season for flirting with Real Madrid. He was heavily booed by Fulham fans in his first appearance in the Premier League as a substitute on Monday night.

That was a reaction to Fernandez’s part in Argentina’s bad tempered win over England in the World Cup semi final.

But, interestingly, Chelsea fans sang his name and Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso also made it clear he wants clarity over Fernandez’s future this week.

‌



View 2 Images Man City are still pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Alonso told the BBC: “In football, I am not surprised by anything. We will see. My wish is that we know what will happen for the future but we will see this week.”

City have been busy in the transfer market and have completed the sale of Savinho - who will be known as Sávio - to Tottenham for £75million without add-ons and are also negotiating a deal with them for Omar Marmoush.

‌



Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders have departed and Nico González could be sold to Newcastle.

They have bought Elliot Anderson, 23, and are bringing in Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille but Maresca is keen for a reunion with Fernandez.

Fernandez helped Chelsea win a European trophy, get back into the Champions League and also win the Club World Cup under Maresca.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes' latest triumph is undisputed proof Man Utd star deserves all the plaudits
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes' latest triumph is undisputed proof Man Utd star deserves all the plaudits

Bruno Fernandes has been crowned as the PFA Player of the Year by his fellow pros - and that is why there should be no backlash like there was after Man Utd star's FWA triumph

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes has been named as the PFA Men's Player of the Year (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

There was a serious backlash in May when Bruno Fernandes won the Football Writers’ Association award as Footballer of the Year.

‌



How can you pick a player who did not win a trophy? What about Declan Rice? Arsenal won the title, after all. It’s just Manchester United bias.

‌



Well, now you have the verdict from the players who probably have a good idea themselves because they have shared a pitch with the contenders. And, once again, the Manchester United captain has come out on top as the Professional Footballers’ Association Player of the Year.

‌



Fernandes did not win a trophy but did break a long-standing record and was, ultimately, the epitome of individual success. The Portugal midfielder registered 21 assists in the Premier League last season which broke the long-standing record jointly held by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

So, actually, it is very fair to say that he also contributed on a team level because he supplied the chances for his United teammates.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



I’ll admit it, I voted for Rice in the FWA awards and, as chair of the Association, I always favour a player who has won a trophy. Can you imagine if Arsenal had won the title and the Champions League? This is 1999 territory when Manchester United won the Treble but David Ginola was crowned Footballer of the Year.

But the fact is they didn’t and the players have spoken - and they voted for Fernandes above the rest.

Furthermore, Fernandes is also such a shining light in the game. Great player, nice personality and was so honoured and thrilled to be crowned FWA Footballer of the Year. You can be sure this latest gong will be just as important and is so richly deserved for one of the very best players in the Premier League.

‌



He is skillful, classy, has great vision and is such a joy to watch. He transformed United’s season last year and this is no more than he deserves.

View 2 Images Fernandes has been recognised for his stellar form last season

The six-strong shortlist from the votes was Rayan Cherki (Manchester City), Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United), Erling Haaland (Manchester City), Gabriel Magalhaes (Arsenal), David Raya (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal).

‌



No wonder City players are in there because they won a domestic cup double in a memorable final season for Pep Guardiola.

But it is so good to see Arsenal represented in great numbers as title winners - and yet no one can argue with Fernandes getting the gong.
