World.title: Croatian Railway Ambitions Tie in With European Defence Efforts
World.content:
August the 25th, 2026 – Croatian railway ambitions are closely linked with European defence efforts, as the country’s “decade of the railway” is still not really being felt on the ground by most.

Any reason for the renewal and development of the railway system in Croatia is very useful, including the security and defence one. But its civilian role remains primary. Index/Deutsche Welle/Igor Lasic reports that following two serious railway traffic incidents at the beginning of this month in Croatia, this mode of passenger and freight transport is once again a topic for the Croatian public.

Moreover, the general public has been reminded of the fact that Croatia is apparently currently in the middle of its “decade of the railway”. This is a state project for the development of this long-neglected mode of transport, with an investment of six billion euros for new tracks and vehicles. Yet despite years of reconstruction, the results are still not really visible on the ground, even though some concrete works have long been planned. The announced “railway renaissance” will therefore clearly still have to wait, and the recent traffic accidents have uncomfortably highlighted this uncertainty.

On top of everything, a new element has been included in the reasoning for the renewal of the Croatian railway sector, and that’s the wider European defence system. Europe is rapidly arming itself, and Croatia has also bought, among other things, more than 40 German Leopard 2 tanks. These, however, because of their exceptional weight, require equally exceptional railway transport capacities. All of this ultimately enters into the final calculation of the development project of the public company Croatian Railways. On the other hand, its relative urgency and the need for centralisation of the system somewhat remove the possibility of imminent privatisation of the sector, which until recently was quite realistic.

so long, privatisation

“Only through the security sphere and social cohesion around the issue of defence have we come to the conclusion that the railway must be managed by the state if we want an efficient system,” Ante Klečina, a railway expert and lecturer at the Department of Sustainable Mobility and Logistics of the University Sjever (North) in Koprivnica and Varaždin, told DW. He referred to the experience of some more developed European countries, such as Great Britain, whose experiments with railway privatisation ended rather ignominiously. Services became of poor quality and too expensive, the system failed in various aspects, and over time it was abandoned.

“First and foremost should be their functionality for civilian needs and, in fact, the organisation of civilisation,” Klečina continues, “which is relevant at every moment if we do not put that priority out of our minds. Whoever swears by the advantages of market mechanisms forgets that they are not developmentally suitable for large public systems, those that enable basic requirements.” In his opinion, the same applies to other elementary systems, e.g. healthcare, education and the judiciary, etc. The private sector, says Klečina, can be a supplement in certain segments, but the backbone must remain public.

“The reason is the necessity of central planning of such systems, as well as their primarily non-profit task, but also the need for enormous investments for which private individuals usually have neither the capacity nor the interest. Having seen this in practice, Europe has recently abandoned the idea of privatising railways, and the defence topic came afterwards as an additional reason,” considers Ante Klečina, formerly president of the Railway Alliance in the Republic of Croatia. He further notes that this mode of transport has no equal with regard to a series of key factors: above all overall cost-effectiveness, economic multiplier effects and environmental suitability.

central planning will always be needed

Socioeconomist Toni Prug, for his part, believes that behind the question of Croatian railways lies the general problem of political and scientific rejection of planning and public production as a relic of the past. That past concerns the period of socialism and Yugoslavia, and everything connected with it remained at the very least stigmatised after the war in Croatia. “In reality, however, all successful states are huge public production systems,” says Prug, “in which planning decides on the largest budgets within economies, on interventions whose importance for the population surpasses the importance of decisions that market actors make.”

This assistant professor at the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences of the University of Rijeka highlights the rule in business that when a market actor makes a mistake, i.e. when things go badly, competition replaces him. “And railways, like all other production systems of a public character that are physically fixed and have monopoly status, need to be carefully planned. Mistakes are much harder to correct. They are also managed differently, different parameters are optimised, a focus on profit does not help. It often cannot even be the goal; the goals are determined by the plan.” At the same time the question arises of whether the Republic of Croatia has the professional staff for designing and implementing this.

“private goals have prevailed over practicality”

“Our profession and managerial staff are educated through faculty and professional curricula that say almost nothing about why and how to produce systems and services of a public character, and why they are superior for certain needs,” Prug is convinced, adding that this knowledge still exists in some Croatian public systems, while in others it has collapsed and been left to spontaneity. In his assessment, the City of Zagreb represents a recent example in Croatia that planning can return and capacities be rebuilt. And on higher-quality, data- and analysis-based foundations, which does not concern the railway but can be a general model.

Toni Prug, who in his scientific work has dealt quite a bit with the topic of public sector management, finally conveyed to us the impression that Croatian Railways have so far been a kind of victim of the oil and automobile lobby. “Their private and profit goals have prevailed over the practicality, efficiency, safety and ecological superiority of modern railway systems,” he told DW. Such a hierarchy could change soon thanks to military priorities. But the future of the railway and of social development in general will certainly not be bright if its primarily civilian advantages remain somewhere beside the tracks.

World.title: Croatia Among European Record Holders for Firefighter Numbers
World.content:
August the 25th, 2026 – Croatia is among the European record holders when it comes to firefighter numbers as the overall number within Europe has fallen.

Poslovni reports that the total number of firefighters across the EU fell from 390,600 in 2024 to 372,400 in 2025, a drop of 18,200 people in a year that was the worst in EU history in terms of burned area.

Croatia is among the European record holders for firefighter numbers, holding one of the highest shares of professional firefighters in employment in the entire EU. Back in 2025, they accounted for 0.43 percent of total employment, making Croatia second among the 22 EU Member States for which data has been made available. This places Croatia right behind Greece (0.47 percent), according to Euronews. The EU average was 0.18 percent. Portugal follows with 0.33 percent, while the lowest shares are recorded by the Netherlands (0.05), Austria (0.07) and Sweden (0.10 percent).

Across the entire EU there were around 372,400 professional firefighters. Germany had the most, 57,700, followed by France with 47,700 and Italy with 43,500. Next come Poland with 40,000 and Spain with 38,500; the four largest EU economies together account for 187,400 firefighters, or 50.3 percent of the total number. The overall figure in the Union fell from 390,600 in 2024 to 372,400 in 2025, a drop of 18,200 people in a single year that was the worst in EU history for burned areas. The European Trade Union Confederation and EPSU call this drop “reckless cuts” and note that Poland lost 9,000 and France lodt 4,100 firefighters.

Croatia doesn’t rank among the leaders in total numbers, but its share of total employment is among the highest. Eurostat data refers to professional firefighters, including forest firefighters, but not volunteer firefighters. The data also doesn’t show precisely how many professional firefighters are specialised specifically in fighting open-air fires.

The data comes at a time when Europe is facing an ever-growing fire risk. According to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) by the 13th of August, the figure had risen to 568,415 hectares from 1,647 fires. For comparison, 2025 was the most destructive season ever recorded in the EU, with 1,079,538 hectares burned in 25 of the 27 EU Member States.

For 2026 the EU has secured a fleet of 22 firefighting aircraft and five helicopters, and in the event of major fires member states can request additional firefighters and equipment through the European Civil Protection Mechanism. In addition, a record 777 firefighters from 14 European countries have been pre-positioned in Cyprus, Greece, Italy, France, Spain and Portugal. Croatia contributes two medium amphibious aircraft to the European fleet, and in 2026 the Commission is also opening a new regional firefighting base in Cyprus with capacity for six aircraft.

World.title: Zadar Was the Most Expensive Croatian City in July
World.content:
August the 24th, 2026 – Zadar was the most expensive Croatian city of all in July, with strong economic growth very much being a double edged sword for the area.

Buying basic groceries has long been a negotiation with one’s own wallet for people in Croatia, but in July, the toughest conditions spilled over onto the area of Zadar County. The basic consumer basket for a four-member family here reached a record 498 euros, reports HRT. Morski writes that a basic daily trip to the shop or the market has become a source of stress for many, and citizens openly complain about the constant quiet price rises:

a previously bustling market sits almost empty

“Vegetables have become very expensive, they get used up quickly, you need a lot of them. Fruit is also very expensive and it seems to me that meat has gone up, fish has also gone up a lot,” says Zadar resident Katja. For pensioners, the situation is even more alarming. Every single purchase requires calculation and a search for discounts: “I really don’t go to the shops much. You buy where you can according to your wallet and that’s it, and yes it’s expensive, it’s definitely expensive, this isn’t for us pensioners, it’s abnormal,” is the honest assessment of Zorica, who lives on the Zagreb–Zadar route.

That consumer habits are changing and that people are buying significantly less than in previous years was confirmed to us by the sellers themselves. Zadar’s market, which in July should be bustling with local and foreign visitors, at times looks unusually empty.

Seller Rada briefly summarises the problem: “Everything is expensive, the shops too.” Her colleague Ilonka points out that even regular customers have thinned out their visits: “There are no customers. I normally have my own customers, but look, two people are walking through the market.”

the price of rapid expansion

How did it come about that Zadar took the top spot for the most expensive groceries? Experts explain that the answer lies in a specific economic effect of the rapid expansion of the regional economy.

Assoc. Prof. Dr. Jurica Bosna, Head of the Department of Economics at the University of Zadar, clarifies the background to this trend: “Nobody wants to have the most expensive basket of goods, but it still shows that the county is developing strongly, and this is an effect known in economics, when we grow faster than we perhaps should according to some optimal economic rates, then it’s unfortunately inevitable that inflation will develop and that the result will be like this,” he stated.

While macroeconomic indicators record the growth and development of the whole of Zadar County, for the general public, that statistic brings no comfort whatsoever. The vicious circle in which the economy advances strongly while prices rise in an unbridled way leaves the deepest mark on household budgets. Since wages and pensions do not come close to keeping pace, the consumer baskets of Zadar residents remain ever emptier.

World.title: Meet the Croatian Road Often Compared to the Legendary Route 66
World.content:
August the 24th, 2026 – There’s an incredibly scenic Croatian road frequently compared to the legendary Route 66 across the pond in the USA – and a drive along it is nothing less than breathtaking.

When someone mentions Route 66, most people immediately think of the endless American highway, old motels, neon signs and kilometres of asphalt running through some of the most famous landscapes of the United States. Few realise that Croatia has its own very interesting road with the same number in Croatia as well. It goes without saying that Croatia’s D66 doesn’t have thousands of kilometres or hold the status of an American icon, but because of the designation it carries and the landscapes it passes through, it resembles the US legend in many ways.

Putni kofer writes that it has been referred to many times as the Istrian version of Route 66 and presented it as a road that evokes old, nostalgic Istria. Today, the impressive D66 connects Pula, Labin and Vozilići with Opatija, and according to the official decision on the classification of public roads it is about 90 kilometres long. Still, if the goal is to find its most spectacular part, one should head towards the eastern coast of Istria, that is, towards Plomin.

the most impressive section begins at plomin

Plomin is an excellent place to start this short road trip. The old fortified little town sits on a hill above Plomin Bay, and right by the D66 there is also a rest area with a viewpoint. A few kilometres further on there is another spot from which the view opens towards the Kvarner Bay, Cres and Lošinj.

After that begins the stretch that makes it worth driving this road slowly. The asphalt winds under the slopes of Učka, the sea is almost constantly somewhere in sight, and on the other side of the Kvarner Cres appears. In certain places the road runs high enough above the coast that the view feels almost like from a large natural balcony. The greatest advantage of state road D66 is precisely that, over a relatively short distance, viewpoints, medieval places, steep coastline and well-known Kvarner resorts alternate.

the stunning Brseč, a town from 1102 towering above at 157 metres above the sea

SONY DSC

One of the places worth turning off the road for is Brseč. D66 reaches it after driving along the slopes of Učka, and the old part of the settlement is situated on a cliff 157 metres high above the expanse of Kvarner. The first written records of Brseč date back to 1102, although the area was inhabited much earlier. It is particularly interesting that the history of Brseč is also directly linked to the road that passes this way. The Tourist Board of Mošćenička Draga notes that the economic development of the place in the 19th century was spurred by the new road from Pula towards Plomin, then Brseč and Mošćenice and further towards Rijeka.

Today the medieval character of Brseč can still be felt in the narrow streets and passages of the old town core. From the cliff by the little church of St Magdalene one of the most beautiful views in the area opens up, while from the western entrance to the place Cres can be seen. Beneath the high rocks a completely different world is hidden. Between Brseč and Mošćenička Draga lie the beaches of Uboka and Jelenšćica, which can be reached on foot via paths that descend from the main road. The coastline in this area is extremely indented, with steep cliffs, tiny coves and stone fishermen’s cottages by the sea.

from ancient towns to well-known resorts

After Brseč the scenery changes again. D66 continues towards Mošćenička Draga, one of the best-known places at the foot of Učka. The road approaches the sea, and the high rocks gradually give way to beaches and a more built-up coastline. Mošćenička Draga developed from a fishing harbour, and today it is especially known for the long pebble beach of Sipar. Its pebbles were formed by the action of the stream that descends from the slopes of Učka and the sea that has shaped them over the years.

Just a few kilometres further on lies Medveja, another place along the D66 with a long pebble beach. After it comes Lovran, where the whole drive takes on a more elegant appearance. Instead of the almost wild coast around Brseč, old villas, gardens and houses appear along the road that recall the time when this part of the Kvarner became one of the favourite resorts of Central Europe.

just over 90 kilometres from pula to opatija

The entire D66 from Pula to Opatija is a little over 90 kilometres long, but for a panoramic outing the stretch from Plomin to Opatija is especially interesting. According to the kilometres listed on the EuroVelo 8 route, from the Plomin area to Opatija it is roughly thirty kilometres of driving.

That may not sound like much, but that is precisely the charm of this road. In a short drive one passes Plomin Bay, open views towards Cres and Lošinj, medieval Brseč, the steep slopes of Učka, Mošćenička Draga, Medveja, Lovran and finally Opatija. Although it forms part of the Croatian cycling route EuroVelo 8, this road should not be imagined as a lonely carriageway without cars. On the official route website traffic on certain sections is marked as moderate, and from Medveja towards Rijeka as heavy, so if you decide to cover it on four wheels, extra caution is recommended for cyclists.

World.title: Drniš Bypass Construction to Benefit Šibenik Port
World.content:
August the 24th, 2026 – The future Drniš bypass will greatly benefit the local economy, as well as Šibenik Port directly.

The construction of the second and third phases of the complex Drniš bypass project has begun, with the client being Hrvatske ceste (Croatian roads), and the contractor being the consortium of Texo Molior from Cavtat and CGP Slovenia.

Transport Minister Butković pointed out that after securing the financial structure and signing the contract, work on the project is now starting. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that he also noted that it is a technically complex intervention with a route that includes two overpasses, two viaducts and a bridge over the Čikola River. Speaking about the continuation of activities on the future Šibenik–Drniš–Knin expressway, Minister Butković highlighted that the preparation of project documentation for the section from Drniš towards the Oklaj interchange is in an advanced stage.

a 34 million euro investment

After the design of that phase is completed, a tender is planned to be issued, so the project is being gradually prepared for phased implementation. He also referred to the reconstruction of state roads DC56 and DC33, which connect the Drniš area with Split and Knin respectively, and whose total reconstruction value is around 34 million euros. After the design of that phase is completed, a tender is planned to be issued, gradually preparing the project for implementation.

“A tender has already been issued for one, the other is in preparation, so there will be a great deal of investment in road infrastructure here in the area of the town of Drniš and Šibenik-Knin County,” added Minister Butković. Šibenik-Knin County Prefect Paško Rakić stressed that the Drniš bypass is of great importance for the entire county, especially for the traffic connection of its hinterland, and that residents of the wider Drniš and Knin areas will use it.

“The Šibenik–Drniš–Knin expressway, as well as this bypass, is the backbone of Šibenik-Knin County in terms of traffic, and it is as important to us as the Pelješac Bridge,” emphasised Prefect Rakić. “This is historic for us,” emphasised Drniš Mayor Tomislav Dželalija, noting that generations of Drniš residents have waited decades for this project.

a massive development boost for the area

Expressing satisfaction that the works were ceremonially started today, he pointed out that the removal of transit traffic, along with increased traffic safety, will create additional preconditions for the expansion of the economic zone and the further development of the town. He added that the Government of the Republic of Croatia, through strong investments including road and railway infrastructure, is giving impetus to the town’s development, and thanked them for the projects being implemented in the Drniš area.

President of the Management Board of Hrvatske ceste Ivica Budimir emphasised that the project has a broader economic significance for Drniš, especially because of the direct connection of the industrial zone with the Šibenik port.

“After this road is constructed, the industrial zone in the entire Drniš area will develop significantly faster, better and to a higher quality, and become much more competitive,” emphasised Budimir. Speaking about the technical demands of the project, he added that almost ten percent of the route consists of viaducts, while the most significant structure is the large bridge over the Čikola River canyon, with a span of 220 metres, along with a series of other structures along the route.

World.title: Baćina Lakes – Meet Croatia’s Freshwater Phenomenon
World.content:
August the 24th, 2026 – Baćina Lakes are Croatia’s freshwater phenomenon, with water warmer than that in the sea and the ability to swim year-round.

If you’ve ever driven from Makarska down toward Dubrovnik, you’ll have passed by them. You probably glanced left for a second, spotted a blue patch amid the greenery, and continued on toward the sea. Yet there, just a few kilometres from Ploče, lies something no other Croatian town has: seven lakes within the boundaries of a single town. They are called the Baćina Lakes and bear names that sound like a list from an old book: Oćuša, Crniševo, Podgora, Sladinac, Šipak, Plitko Lake, and Vrbnik.

Putni kofer writes that six of them are interconnected by narrow passages, so you can paddle or boat from one into another, while Vrbnik, which is also the smallest, is completely separate from the rest. Together they cover about 138 hectares.

they’re warmer than the sea

The Baćina Lakes form a cryptodepression, meaning their surface is only slightly above sea level, while their bottoms lie deep below it. Although they are just a step from the sea and surrounded by permeable limestone, the lakes are freshwater. Some springs are nevertheless directly connected to the sea, so salt water appears in the deeper layers. In the Klokun area near Plitko Lake there is a spring that supplies drinking water to the town of Ploče and the surrounding area.

During the scorching summer, the water in the lakes is noticeably warmer than the sea, with tourist sources citing a difference of roughly three degrees. Because of this, the swimming season here starts earlier and ends later than on the coast. The best-known bathing spots are those near the Mindel spring, and the hidden coves and small beaches are reached by kayak, paddleboard, or traditional Neretva boat.

links with queen teuta

Legend has it that the Illyrian Queen Teuta adored this area, and the lakes are still called Teuta’s pearls. Historians, however, have their own evidence and explanations. Near Sladinac Lake the remains of the Roman settlement of Praetoria have been found, along with the remains of an early Christian basilica from the 6th century and a necropolis of stećci tombstones.

Around the lakes a walking and cycling path about 15 kilometres long has been arranged, with benches, springs, and information boards. In 2020 the Public Institution for Protected Natural Areas of Dubrovnik-Neretva County installed 19 educational boards about dragonflies, amphibians, reptiles, and birds. Near the Oćuša spring there is a bird-watching hide, and the lakes also contain three small islets, one of which is named the Island of Love. The entire area forms part of the Natura 2000 ecological network, within two zones of the Neretva Delta, as a habitat for strictly protected and endemic species.

a worthwhile stop off on a long drive south…

A visit to the Baćina Lakes is truly an experience you will remember for a lifetime. Walking the paths that wind right beside the lakes will reveal scenes covered in water lilies, the reflection of clouds mirrored on the still water, and the song of rare birds that creates an almost meditative atmosphere.

Here you can also swim in crystal-clear water that provides refreshment during the great heat, and a special experience comes when the sun sets and the whole landscape is immersed in golden and pink tones. Then the lakes take on an almost fairy-tale appearance. It is a perfect moment for a photograph, but also for simply enjoying the silence of nature.

In the heart of the summer season, a parking space at the viewpoint along the main road is almost impossible to find. Down by the lakes themselves, however, there are usually no crowds. Most travellers photograph the view and drive on, while those who go down to the water, sit in a boat, or cycle a loop are completely enchanted and, like us, probably think: “How is this place not far better known?”

World.title: Vanemuine and the Latvian National Opera swap stages for guest performances this week
World.content:
A guest‑performance exchange between the national theatre Vanemuine and the Latvian National Opera and Ballet begins on Tuesday in Tartu and Riga.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, audiences at Vanemuine's Grand Building can see two guest productions from Latvia. On Tuesday, 25 August, the Latvian National Opera presents Gaetano Donizetti's "L'elisir d'amore", staged by Austrian director Sven‑Eric Bechtolf. The musical director of the production is Mārtiņš Ozoliņš, chief conductor of the Latvian National Opera.

On Wednesday, 26 August, a full house will see Carl Orff's ballet "Carmina Burana", choreographed by Edward Clug, whose short ballet "The Rite of Spring" premiered this spring at Vanemuine. The production brings together the Latvian National Ballet, the Latvian National Opera orchestra and choir, and opera soloists.

In Riga, Vanemuine will perform three productions for Latvian audiences. The tour begins on 27 August at the Dailes Theatre with the drama "The End". On 28 August, the Latvian National Opera hosts Petr Zuska's dance‑music‑theatre piece "Prayer. A Tribute to Arvo Pärt", inspired by the composer's music. On 29 August, audiences will see George Frideric Handel's baroque opera "Julius Caesar", directed by Elmo Nüganen.

Vanemuine director Aivar Mäe said the cooperation is a true cultural bridge between Estonia and Latvia. "One should not wait for the world to come visiting — one must also set out on the road. Vanemuine must stay in motion. And on this bridge, traffic goes both ways," he said.

World.title: Prosecutor's Office expands Isamaa party illicit funding suspicions
World.content:
Isamaa remains suspected of accepting prohibited donations as a criminal investigation into the party enters the final stage of pretrial proceedings, though the party maintains it has done nothing wrong.

As the latest procedural step, the Prosecutor's Office amended the notice of suspicion issued to Isamaa.

"The defense attorneys for the suspects are currently reviewing the materials in the criminal case and have one month to submit motions," said Chief State Prosecutor Taavi Pern. He added that a decision can then be made on whether to bring charges and send the case to court.

Under the law, only private individuals may make donations to political parties and such donations must be reported to the Political Parties Financing Surveillance Committee (ERJK).

Lawmakers have stipulated that legal entities, such as companies and nonprofit organizations, may not donate to political parties because doing so makes it easy to conceal the true donors and render party financing opaque.

According to the Central Criminal Police's notice of suspicion, two legal entities provided Isamaa with nearly €308,000 worth of services, primarily advertising services, between 2020 and 2023, for which the party did not pay.

The costs associated with the services were also not reflected in the party's financial reports, nor were the services declared to ERJK as donations.

According to the notice of suspicion, some of the party's senior members or representatives knew that the legal entities were acting for the party's benefit, accepted this and used the benefits received in the party's interests. Isamaa is therefore suspected of accepting a prohibited donation.

Pern said that six individuals and three legal entities were initially named as suspects in the criminal case. The Prosecutor's Office terminated the investigation into one of the suspects, Mart Maastik, after finding no evidence of a possible offense in his actions.

Suspicions expanded

According to Isamaa Secretary General Andres Metsoja, there is nothing new in the notice of suspicion.

"In the first version of the notice of suspicion, the entire €330,000 in question was not attributed to Isamaa as allegedly constituting the acceptance of a prohibited donation," Metsoja said.

Metsoja said he believes no new circumstances have emerged, even though the case has been under investigation since March.

"Now they are saying that Isamaa allegedly accepted a prohibited donation on a larger scale," Metsoja explained. "We want to establish exactly what circumstances they are referring to again or additionally."

"For us, this means a large amount of material that needs to be reviewed. Isamaa continues to maintain that we have not accepted anything prohibited. The scope and extent of the notice of suspicion remain the same as they were initially; only the details have been clarified," Metsoja said.

The secretary general said he has met with the investigator and clearly stated that Isamaa does not consider itself guilty of any wrongdoing.

He added that Isamaa will review the materials and will certainly submit additional questions to seek clarification.

"The most important thing is that one suspect, Mart Maastik, has been removed from the proceedings and is no longer a suspect," Metsoja said.

Metsoja said he does not know why the proceedings against Maastik were terminated. "We will also seek the termination of proceedings against Isamaa and the other parties involved," he said.

World.title: Saue Municipality E. coli water contamination source still unknown
World.content:
The source and extent of E. coli contamination in Saue Municipality remains unknown, with local government and the state carrying out joint sampling and investigations.

Some residents have reported severe health issues, and water from private bore wells in the suspected zone is not fit for drinking or brushing teeth, though public supply is unaffected.

The state Health Board (Terviseamet) is investigating reported illnesses to establish a link with the contamination. Work is underway to locate the source and prevent further contamination, while also delineating the affected zones.

Last weekend, local government and Environmental Board officials inspected on-site wastewater treatment systems in the northwestern area of the municipality, southwest of Tallinn, between Kivipõllu and the railway line to the west. Up to 40 systems have been inspected, and the municipality says the "overall picture is not good," with some systems failing to meet required standards. However, there are currently no grounds to conclude that any of these caused the contamination.

Drinking water has been set up for local residents affected by the contamination. Source: ERR

The situation is complicated by the fact that the speed and direction of contamination spread cannot be precisely determined. Ongoing construction work on Rauna tänav is also being investigated as a possible source.

A crisis committee convened Monday and has opted to continue efforts to determine the cause. Additional water samples will be taken from a wider area — not because the contamination zone has expanded, but to obtain a more accurate picture of groundwater quality and possible spread.

In the meantime, public fresh drinking water tanks have been made available in those areas affected.

World.title: Guilty verdict stands in Pärnu water park drowning case
World.content:
A court ruling over a 2023 drowning death at a Pärnu spa center has taken effect, with one defendant handed a year and three months' prison time in suspended sentence.

June's second-tier Tallinn Circuit Court's guilty verdict entered into force in respect of the Tervise Paradiis water park in Pärnu and Gert Kuusik, who worked there as a lifeguard.

Both the club and the lifeguard were found guilty of causing death by negligence, and while they had appealed the ruling, the Supreme Court declined to hear it.

The circuit court sentenced Kuusik to one year and three months in prison, suspended if Kuusik commits no further offense during a probationary period of one year and six months.

OÜ Tervise Paradiis was fined €50,000 as a result of the ruling.

On March 11, 2023, a man drowned at the water park in Pärnu after being pushed into a four-meter-deep pool. According to the charges, the visitor found himself in distress but did not receive timely assistance that may have saved his life. More specifically, prosecutors accused Tervise Paradiis's senior lifeguard of assigning a staff member who was regularly employed in an administrative capacity to deputize for an absent lifeguard, despite that replacement employee lacking the training and skills required of the job.

The ruling followed an appeal from the Prosecutor's Office after the first-tier Pärnu County Court acquitted Tervise Paradiis and Gert Kuusik in January 2025.

Initially the Tallinn Circuit Court upheld the acquittal, but the ruling was appealed to the Supreme Court by the prosecutor, and on rehearing the case the guilty verdict was reached. The defendants' appeal to the Supreme Court was rejected, meaning the circuit court judgment is now in force.

New lifeguard rules were announced for all pools from January 2026, widely seen as a response to the case.

World.title: Tallinn Fringe Festival continues into 2nd week with international program
World.content:
The annual Tallinn Fringe Festival is into its second week, with an international itinerary bringing theater, Icelandic cabaret and Irish street performances to the capital.

The Irish street performances, taking place in Town Hall Square (Raekoja plats), are free to watch and are supported by Cultúr Éireann and the Embassy of Ireland in Estonia.

The open‑access Fringe format means performances take place in theaters, bars and other spaces across the city, which organizers say allows visitors to create their own festival experiences. This week's program includes theater, stand‑up comedy, burlesque, circus, street performances, cabaret and classical music.

Week one's highlights included festival director Dan Renwick complete the first of two half‑marathons in Helsinki on August 22 — all while juggling. In total, Renwick will be running/juggling 42.2 kilometers in support of the festival, with the second half‑marathon taking place on September 9 as part of the Tallinn Marathon weekend. The challenge aims to raise funds towards the festival's overall €20,000 fundraising goal.

Artist George Fenn (New Zealand), who performed at the festival, said: "Fringe festivals are essential incubators for all kinds of art forms that don't yet have the support of larger organizations or established funding systems. Their open‑access model gives creators the opportunity to take greater risks. Fringe festivals also have a major positive impact on the local economy."

This is the 10th Tallinn Fringe Festival and it runs until September 18. The full program and tickets are available on the Tallinn Fringe website.

World.title: Banks say Estonia's economy strengthens as domestic demand rises, inflation eases
World.content:
Estonia's economy is gaining momentum, with Swedbank and SEB reporting stronger domestic demand, easing inflation and improving export prospects in forecasts published August 25.

Swedbank forecasts Estonia's real GDP to grow 2.0 percent in 2026 and 2.5 percent in 2027, with inflation easing to 3.4 percent this year and 2.7 percent next year.

Swedbank senior economist Liis Elmik: "We have revised this year's inflation forecast downward because recent monthly inflation figures have been more modest than expected, especially for food prices. Food has fallen quite significantly in recent months."

Elmik added that energy plays the biggest role in this year's inflation forecast.

Liis Elmik. Source: ERR

"Everyone has likely noticed that motor fuels have become more expensive. After the start of the Middle East war, oil prices rose sharply. Gas prices did not react immediately at first, but they are now also climbing, and our forecast is based on futures prices for both oil and gas. Those show that gas prices this winter will be higher than in recent years," she said.

Rising real income and a stronger labor market are lifting Estonia's household spending, while investment is expected to pick up as confidence improves, said Swedbank Economic Outlook, published on August 25. The government continues to channel major resources into defense and infrastructure, but faces a significant challenge in improving public finances.

Recently updated GDP data show Estonia's economy contracted for only one year, in 2023, instead of the previously estimated three‑year period from 2022 to 2024. Preliminary figures indicate the economy grew 1.6 percent in the first half of 2026.

Domestic demand has been the main driver of growth this year in Estonia and is expected to remain a key engine next year. Private consumption has increased as household purchasing power has strengthened.

Government consumption and investment have also become important contributors to growth. Higher defense spending and infrastructure investment are adding momentum to domestic demand.

Private investment is expected to strengthen despite weak quarterly national accounts earlier this year. Lending activity has remained strong even as interest rates have edged higher. By June, Swedbank's mortgage loan portfolio growth had accelerated to about 10 percent year‑on‑year, while corporate lending expanded even more. Strong loan demand reflects improving confidence among households and businesses.

Swedbank headquarters in Tallinn. Source: Mait Ots / ERR

Swedbank expects economic growth among Estonia's trading partners to improve this year and next, boosting foreign demand.

"Finland is Estonia's largest trading partner; we export 15 percent of our goods and services there," said Swedbank economist Tõnu Mertsina. "In addition to being our biggest trading partner, Estonia's goods exports to Finland are also among the most broad‑based. So when demand in Finland improves, it gives our export sector more opportunities to sell there. In turn, that has a positive impact on Estonia's economy."

Competitiveness remains a challenge in Estonia. Labor costs continue to rise faster than productivity, keeping cost pressures high and limiting gains in competitiveness. Unit labor costs in manufacturing have increased more in Estonia than in many of its major trading partners.

Fiscal stimulus has played a major role in Estonia's recovery, especially this year, but has also widened the budget deficit. Fiscal policy is likely to remain broadly unchanged until the next parliamentary elections in March 2027, leaving more comprehensive decisions on public finances to the next government, Swedbank said.

SEB expects 2.5 percent growth this year

Estonia's economy is developing largely as expected and is on track to grow 2.5 percent in 2026, SEB bank said in its Nordic Outlook published August 25.

Households are benefiting from tax cuts that have lifted disposable incomes, while stronger investment and a brighter export outlook are expected to push growth close to 3 percent in 2027 and 2028. SEB noted that the high‑growth years before the pandemic appear to be over and that sustaining growth above 3 percent will require new drivers.

Consumers are leading the recovery. A major upward revision to first‑quarter GDP confirms the economy has entered a rebound. Growth so far has been driven mainly by household consumption, which had previously been held back by higher taxes, interest rates, inflation and weak confidence.

Mihkel Nestor. Source: Kairit Leibold/ERR

This year, households have instead gained from tax cuts that boosted disposable incomes, especially for higher earners, while inflation has fallen to about 2 percent. SEB expects consumption growth to moderate as these effects fade.

SEB economic analyst Mihkel Nestor says that unfortunately, stronger growth figures are not reflected in what people think about the economy — consumer confidence remains very low.

"There are likely many reasons why people do not believe in a brighter future: geopolitical tensions, large swings in commodity prices, painful memories of tax hikes and inflation, and more. One aspect that has not been discussed so far is the simple fact that Estonians have become accustomed to faster growth than today's economy can deliver. From 2010 to 2019, Estonia's GDP grew by nearly 4 percent a year on average. Those days are over and will likely never return," Nestor noted.

Inflation pressures have eased. The outlook remains sensitive to energy and food prices, but domestic price pressures have softened. Barring external shocks, inflation is expected to stay relatively stable at around 2.5 percent throughout the forecast period.

Seb Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi /ERR

The export outlook has improved sharply, driven by stronger‑than‑expected growth among Estonia's main trading partners. The turnaround in Finland, Estonia's largest export market, is particularly notable, with growth returning sooner than expected. SEB said this should ease pressure on the manufacturing sector, which has faced difficult conditions for several years.

Investment is becoming a key growth driver and is expected to deliver the largest positive surprises in the coming years. Much of the momentum is coming from major public projects, including Rail Baltica and increased defense spending, but private‑sector investment is also strengthening.

The labor market remains stable. The employment rate for people aged 15–74 is close to 70 percent, leaving limited room for further gains. Wage growth is expected to ease somewhat but remain above 5 percent throughout the forecast period.

Economic issues are expected to dominate the debate ahead of the parliamentary elections in March 2027. Criticism of the large budget deficit and rapidly rising public debt has intensified.

SEB noted that while parties recognize the challenge, solutions are difficult: defense spending accounts for a large share of the increase, and further tax hikes would be politically hard after several previous increases. Some parties have pledged to abolish the unpopular motor vehicle tax or cut VAT on food, but delivering on such promises would be difficult under current fiscal constraints.

World.title: Parents should take children's back-to-school anxiety seriously, expert says
World.content:
With the new academic year arriving next week, parents should be careful not to minimize anxiety their children may have about the back-to-school period, an expert said.

Minna Kruus, a psychologist with youth mental health support organization Peaasi.ee, told "R2 päev" that the anxiety should be taken seriously, as roots could include bullying and other real concerns.

Estimates put the number of returning school pupils experiencing significant anxiety at up to half, though this relates to the entire school year and not simply the end of the summer holidays period. Anxiety specifically related to the start of the academic year has not been measured separately, Kruus said, though what is known is that the number of calls to the child helpline on 116 111 see a spike in late August, indicating a rise in anxiety levels among school-age children.

This is the case "especially with younger children, they may not even realize it themselves," Kruus noted. "It may manifest as more frequent stomach aches, feeling unwell, being down, or perhaps difficulty falling asleep," she explained.

This is not to say a certain degree of anticipation or of being unsettled on the eve of the new school year is unnatural, Kruus went on.

All parents should talk about this with their child and, where needed, relate their own school experiences. If parents can find out what exactly is bothering the child, it can clarify whether it is simply ordinary back-to-school anxiety or something more concerning.

Minna Kruus. Source: ERR

"Many children may actually have a very real reason. There is something at school that causes greater discomfort, perhaps fear," she noted. Bullying is sometimes the root cause.

If a child is dreading the start of the new school year, a parent can help break the problem down into smaller chunks, Kruus noted. Together, they can think through back-to-school routines taking in sleeping, eating, and other everyday activities, as well as study and school activities. A family or household with more than one child in school might also do well to hold a home meeting, to discuss what kind of support each person needs, the expert added.

When a child flatly states they do not want to go back to school, their feelings should be empathized with. However, according to Kruus, avoiding school outright is not an ideal solution, she said, and magnifies the issue. "In that case, the feeling of anxiety only grows, or it sort of wins that battle," she said, stressing a feel-the-fear-and-do-it-anyway approach. "Anxiety is with us, but then again our courage is with us too," Kruus put it.

The start of the new school year can bring stress to parents too. Kruus said caregivers should try to regulate their own feelings and not pass on their worries to their child. They can certainly tell the child that they, too, feel anxious about the start of school, but not stray too far beyond that; parents should never start burdening the child with their own concerns and anxieties, Kruus said.

"They are still the adult, who bears even greater responsibility for their feelings than the child does," she stressed.

Young people of junior high school age through to young adults (ages 12 to 26) can approach Peaasi.ee for help. The organization can teach skills for coping with anxiety and help with lifestyle choices. The Peaasi.ee site in English is here.

The child helpline is 116 111. English-speaking operators are available.

World.title: Expert: New government powers give the Kremlin more control over the Russian economy
World.content:
Russian leader Vladimir Putin on Monday authorized the government to take control of privately owned critical infrastructure if it is deemed inadequately protected against Ukrainian attacks and other threats.

The special powers introduced by Putin's order allow the state to take control of the physical assets, financial assets and legal rights of such facilities if they fail to provide adequate protection or are too slow to repair damage following attacks.

Putin's order covers a wide range of sectors, including fuel, energy and industrial facilities, communications and transportation infrastructure, as well as commercial logistics facilities considered essential to national security and economic stability.

The new powers were introduced a week after Putin ordered the government to help restore warehouses belonging to online retailers that had been damaged in Ukrainian attacks.

Since the beginning of the summer, Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian oil refineries and, increasingly, on warehouses and logistics centers belonging to major e-commerce companies Wildberries and Ozon.

According to Raivo Vare, an analyst who follows the Russian economy, Putin's decision has two important implications.

"First, the private owners operating in this sector can no longer keep things running purely on market principles, using loans that they can no longer afford to take out and that are no longer being offered to them, and they can no longer manage it from a technical standpoint either," Vare said.

Vare said the move was driven by necessity because the ownership structures of the companies include people with extremely close ties to the Kremlin who need assistance. He noted, for example, that Wildberries has been linked to Anton Vaino, chief of staff of the Presidential Executive Office, as well as Dagestani billionaire and Federation Council member Suleiman Kerimov.

Second, Vare said the situation also provides the Kremlin with a favorable opportunity to expand state control.

"Let's put it this way: In a situation where your hand is forced, you can resolve matters simply, cheaply and, so to speak, conveniently because the renationalization campaign in Russia has already been underway for quite some time and is now beginning to grow in scale," Vare said. "Previously, it targeted medium-sized companies, but now large companies are also in line — agricultural businesses, mining companies and so on."

Raivo Vare. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Vare said very specific interest groups are behind the expansion of state control.

"Because Russia faces extensive restrictions abroad and businesses can no longer expand internationally or make money there, the stronger players are redistributing assets domestically in their own favor and that is actually being partly concealed by this renationalization," Vare said.

Since July 18, Kyiv has attacked at least 20 warehouses belonging to Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, destroying a large share of the company's warehousing capacity.

On Monday, Ozon, Russia's second-largest online retailer, said four of its facilities in southern Russia had been targeted in Ukrainian attacks.

Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov said the measure should not be viewed as a first step toward nationalization and would not be widely applied.

"This does not mean nationalization or a change in ownership. The decree allows the state to participate in a company's management in order to address specific security issues," Interfax quoted Manturov as saying.

World.title: Iraq to allocate $15 billion for delayed projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq plans to allocate 20 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $15 billion) in its draft 2027 budget primarily to complete delayed projects while entirely blocking funds for new projects.

The state budget approach indicates a clear shift toward performance-based expenditure, cost savings, and meeting long-term infrastructure obligations.

The entire capital expenditure portion of the budget focuses on revitalizing infrastructure. Mazhar Saleh, the financial adviser to Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, stated in an interview with Iraq’s official newspaper al-Sabah that there will be no funding allocated for new development projects.

The proposed budget offers a low-risk average oil price target of $60 to $70 per barrel.

Hospitals, schools, bridges, tunnels, and water networks are among the critical public services targeted by the multibillion-dollar commitment.

Following the decision to skip a formal 2026 budget due to regional disturbances, the Iraqi parliament’s financial committee anticipates the official 2027 draft being submitted for approval between late October and early November 2026.

While focusing on current projects gives a more direct path to infrastructure improvement, Iraq is reorganizing its budget due to severe financial pressures.

The Iraqi Ministry of Finance is working with the World Bank to shift from traditional line-item expenditure to a program-and-performance approach.

Iraq’s budget deficit exceeded 21 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $16.1 billion) in the first half of the year due to huge governmental payroll expenditures. As a result, more than 1,800 development projects have been canceled or suspended.

Military operations in the region and shipping restrictions via the Strait of Hormuz have slashed marine crude exports, which account for more than 85 percent of state revenue.

To secure cash for the 2027 budget, Baghdad has allowed three-month temporary marketing mechanisms to diversify export outlets and is focusing on pipelines through Turkey and Syria to increase oil exports.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate slightly falls against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight decline on Tuesday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,543.5 Iraqi dinars on Tuesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,537.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,544.5 and 1,543.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq, Germany discuss international coalition withdrawal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Commander of German Forces Deployed Abroad, Gunter Schneider, met on Monday in Baghdad to organize the US-led international coalition forces’ imminent withdrawal from Iraq.

The meeting addressed strategies to strengthen bilateral relations between Iraq and Germany in the military and security fields through initiatives aiming to improve the performance of the Iraqi armed forces, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister stressed the need to develop broader partnerships with the international coalition’s member countries. He praised Germany for aiding Iraq in its battle against terrorism, notably during the confrontation with ISIS.

Al-Zaidi said earlier that the military mission of the international coalition will expire on September 30, 2026, and that the decision is final and irreversible.

The prime minister underscored that October 1 will bring in a new period of total Iraqi independence and full territorial sovereignty, with no foreign military presence.

Iraq’s future interactions with the international coalition’s member states will focus on direct security, economic, and specialized training cooperation based on mutual respect.

The international coalition was first formed in 2014 to combat the emergence of the terrorist group ISIS.

After Iraq declared military victory over ISIS in 2017, international coalition forces continued to provide advice and training services at Baghdad’s request.

The official withdrawal of the international coalition follows a bilateral arrangement agreed upon by Baghdad and Washington.

World.title: Nasiriyah International Airport reaches 68% completion, targets early 2027 opening
World.content:
Nasiriyah (IraqiNews.com) — Construction work on the Nasiriyah International Airport project in Dhi Qar Governorate has reached a 68% overall completion rate, according to statements made on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, by Captain Ihab Saad, Director General of the General Company for Airports Management and Air Navigation Services.

Saad characterized the construction momentum as continuous and accelerating, confirming that the facility is projected for official delivery in early 2027, provided current construction schedules proceed without unforeseen disruptions.

Technical Milestones & Equipment Inspection

Current Progress: Civil and structural engineering works stand at 68% completion.

Ground Handling Systems: Progress rates are set to increase significantly upon the delivery and installation of new ground handling and airfield equipment batches.

Factory Acceptance Testing in China: A specialized technical committee is traveling to China to conduct rigorous factory acceptance tests on navigational, baggage, and ground operations equipment prior to on-site installation.

Contractual Adjustments: Project authorities have resolved primary operational bottlenecks and are finalizing a new contract appendix to formally settle remaining technical and logistical requirements.

The foundation stone for Nasiriyah International Airport was laid in June 2021 to serve as a major commercial and logistics hub for southern Iraq:

International Contractors: In mid-July 2024, the Ministry of Transport finalized a consultancy and design contract appendix with Turkish firm Kiklop Design Hertz Insaat, alongside an amended engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract with China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC).

Delivery Schedule Evolution: Following earlier timeline revisions from late 2025 into early 2026, project management has established early 2027 as the targeted commissioning window to accommodate factory testing, equipment integration, and final aviation certification.

Upon completion, Nasiriyah International Airport will serve as a critical gateway for passenger transit, business investment, and cultural tourism in Dhi Qar, providing direct international connectivity to the ancient city of Ur, the Mesopotamian Marshes (Ahwar), and surrounding southern industrial zones.

World.title: Iraq continues to be South Korea’s fourth-largest oil supplier
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq was the fourth largest crude oil supplier to South Korea in the first half of 2026, accounting for 7.4 percent of the country’s total oil imports.

According to the Korea Petroleum Association (KPA) and the Korea National Oil Corporation, South Korea imported 467.12 million barrels of crude oil in the first half of the year, an eight percent decline compared to the same period in 2025.

However, the value of the country’s oil imports increased by 8.1 percent to $41.36 billion as global oil prices surged, local news outlet Shafaq News reported.

Saudi Arabia was the largest supplier of oil to South Korea, making up 30.5 percent of the country’s total oil imports. The United States followed with over 20 percent of South Korea’s crude oil imports.

Oil supplies from the United Arab Emirates accounted for 15.1 percent of South Korea’s oil imports.

The figures indicate a notable shift in South Korea’s oil supplies, with Middle Eastern oil falling from 68.7 percent to 62.3 percent throughout the time. This shift is basically due to the effects of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which caused interruptions in oil supplies worldwide.

Iraq’s average oil shipments to South Korea totaled 113.7 million barrels in 2025, which is an average of 311,500 barrels per day. This represents a 12 percent increase compared to 2024.

World.title: U.S. prepares to return diplomats to Iraq and Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The United States is preparing to return evacuated foreign service personnel to several diplomatic missions across the Middle East, according to an internal U.S. State Department document and confirmations from three U.S. officials reported by The New York Times on Tuesday, August 25, 2026.

The decision indicates that Washington does not anticipate a return to full-scale regional hostilities following recent conflict escalations, despite stalled direct talks between Washington and Tehran and renewed threats of economic sanctions.

Phased Staffing Levels by Mission

The State Department’s operational plan outlines specific staffing quotas and regional safety parameters:

Iraq, Kuwait, and Bahrain: Restoring on-site diplomatic staff up to 75% capacity.

UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Lebanon: Restoring on-site personnel up to 85% capacity, with Lebanon receiving some of the earliest returnees.

Israel, Jordan, and Oman: Authorizing a 100% full return of diplomatic personnel.

Dependent Travel Restrictions: Washington will maintain strict restrictions on accompanying family members across Lebanon and all six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, reflecting a calibrated security posture where overall threat levels have declined relative to the peak of the conflict but remain elevated compared to baseline conditions.

The planned return follows progressive emergency evacuations initiated in late February and early March 2026:

Pre-Strike Precautionary Moves: In late February 2026, non-essential personnel and family members at the U.S. mission in Jerusalem were offered voluntary departure immediately preceding joint military operations.

Baghdad Evacuations and Standoff: In early March 2026, the State Department ordered the mandatory drawdown of non-emergency staff across regional posts, including Baghdad, ahead of drone and rocket strikes targeting the U.S. Embassy compound on March 17.

Ceasefire Dynamics: While a 60-day ceasefire expired last week without formal renewal terms finalized, U.S. security assessments determined that resuming partial mission staffing balances operational foreign policy objectives with on-ground personnel safety.

Former U.S. diplomatic and defense officials noted that while redeploying personnel underscores an administrative assessment that active war footing is receding, emergency contingency mechanisms remain in place should regional security dynamics shift.

World.title: Congress’s pellet gun fire draws BJP 1984 counter
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Demand from opposition MPs, including

, that a parliamentary committee take up the issue of use of âexcessiveâ force against protesting students led to a fiery exchange at its meeting on Tuesday as a BJP member brought up the âglorificationâ of anti-Sikh riots convict Sajjan Kumar to counter the Congressâs move to raise a matter that was not part of the agenda of âcrimes against childrenâ.

Sources said Congress MP Ajay Maken had written to parliamentary committee on home affairs chairperson and BJP MP Radha Mohan Das Agrawal on Aug 5 saying the discussion should include the allegations against the Delhi Police that its personnel used pellet guns and nail-fitted batons against protesting students during their march to Parliament on July 20. As the committee met, Maken raised the issue and was supported by a number of other opposition MPs, including Priyanka and Senta UBTâs Sanjay Raut.

They said the Delhi Police chief should be asked to appear before the committee, insisting that the issue fell within the ambit of crimes against children.

Agrawal said the matter is sub judice. With opposition MPs pressing their demand, BJP MP Tarun Chugh said that if members are allowed to raise issues not on the agenda, then he would like the committee to take up the alleged glorification of a Sikh-riots convict, a reference to former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar who died last week while serving his sentence.

Chughâs remarks drew a sharp reaction from Congress MP Jai Prakash, who said the issue was not relevant at all. BJP has accused Congress MP Deepender Hooda of being laudatory in his tribute to Kumar. Hooda has rejected the charge. Agrawal managed to restore order while ruling out a discussion on issues not on the agenda, even as he added that the committee would take up at a later date the issue of SOPs for the use of force against protesters.

World.title: All Banke Bihari donations must go to deity: Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The SC Tuesday took strong exception to the report of the court-appointed high-powered committee (HPC) headed by a retired HC judge that donations at Banke Bihari temple at Vrindavan are being pocketed by sevayats and ordered that devoteesâ contributions must go only to the temple.

Senior advocate Maninder Singh said the sevayats cover the donation box put up by the temple management committee with flowers to prevent devotees from putting their donations into it. These donations are then taken away by the sevayats, he said.

Brushing aside the counselâs submissions that a court decree allows sevayats to keep a part of the donations, a CJI-led bench said all donations must be deposited in temple donation boxes or credited online into the temple account. âFirst, the donation must be into the dedication, i.e., to the deity. From that you will get your share as part of âbhandariâ duties.â

World.title: Revised bullet train cost Rs 2 lakh crore, 2x of original estimate
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The cost of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai bullet train has been revised to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore, nearly double the original cost of approximately Rs 1.1 lakh crore. The proposal to seek approval for the revised cost of the 508-km high-speed rail line was placed before the Cabinet Tuesday, TOI has learnt.

Sources said the railway ministry has cited the time taken in land acquisition in Maharashtra and delay in getting the train sets from Japan as among the main reasons for the cost escalation. They added the project is likely to be completed in 2030 and the first leg of the corridor is scheduled to be operational in Aug 2027.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Sources said most of the additional funding would come from budgetary support. So far, the funding of Rs 1.1 lakh crore has been from Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and budgetary allocation. They added that Railways has said high-speed trains will be manufactured in India and each of these would cost around Rs 390 crore to Rs 400 crore. There was no official briefing on the decisions of the Cabinet meeting chaired by PM

.

In Jan, railway board chairperson Satish Kumar had said the project cost had increased by around 83% to Rs 1.98 lakh crore. The project has faced time and cost overruns due to many reasons, including delay in land acquisition, statutory clearances and finalisation of the trains.

World.title: NMC pushes old doctors to re-register, but can’t net new ones
World.content:
National Medical Commission (NMC) is seeking to re-register around 11 lakh doctors to create an updated national medical registry, yet it has failed to register even fresh entrants to the profession despite many state registries sharing records every year, reports Rema Nagarajan.

Based on MBBS seats and pass rates, at least 68,000 new doctors should have registered to practice, but only 44,400 entries were recorded in 2025 with at least 24,000 graduates missing in Indian Medical Register. The gap points to potential failure of NMC to sync state and national registries, as required under NMC Act.

NMC pushes old docs to re-register, but canât net new ones

The National Medical Commission (NMC) is pushing a regulation to make about 11 lakh doctors re-register to create an updated national medical registry, but it has failed to even register fresh entrants to the profession despite many state registries sending it new entries every year.

With over 91,000 MBBS seats available in 2020-21, even with an estimated 75-90% pass percentage, at least 68,000 MBBS graduates should have registered to practice in 2025. Yet the Indian Medical Register shows just over 44,400 entries. That means at least 24,000 of those who graduated just last year are missing from the registry.

If thousands of foreign medical graduates who register each year are included, the number of freshly minted doctors missing from the registry would be even more.





For instance, in 2023, over 10,000 foreign medical graduates passed the qualifying exam, after which they have to complete a mandatory one-year internship before receiving permanent registration that would make them eligible to practice in India. So, most of these 10,000 would have registered in 2025.

Thus, the total number of doctors registering in 2025 would be roughly 80,000, but just over half the number (55%) have been added to the registry.

Most of the doctors would have registered with state medical councils. However, new entries in state medical council registries are not being reflected in the national registry as the NMC is yet to synchronise all state registries with the national registry. The NMC Act, 2019, had mandated such synchronisation. It is yet to happen, almost six years after the NMC was constituted in Sept 2020. Neither is NMC adding the new entries that many state councils send every year.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Take Assam Medical Council, for instance. It is a state with only govt medical colleges. In the national registry, there are a total of 25,722 registrations from the state council. It shows only one entry for 2025, zero for 2024 and 2023, 106 entries for 2022 and 353 in 2021. The website shows 890 registered in 2024. There were over 720 seats in Assam in 2015 and 1,000 seats in 2020. How is NMC accepting zero entries in 2023 and 2024, or only 106 in 2022?

Similarly, NMCâs registry has a total of 67,142 entries from Kerala with just seven entries in 2025 and 17 in 2024. In 2014, Kerala had 3,650 MBBS seats, which increased to 4,500 by 2020. âWe are sending details every year... In the name of a new updated NMR, they are not updating the existing one,â said KSMC chief Dr Harikumaran Nair.

If the NMC were to register only those who became doctors in the last five years, including foreign medical graduates, it would have had an updated registry of over 3.5 lakh doctors (32%) of the estimated 11 lakh who are said to be available.

World.title: Govt seeks 2 years to frame creamy layer criteria for PSU, private staff kids
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Seeking two years to frame creamy layer criteria for OBCs, Centre Tuesday requested Supreme Court for an early hearing on its application against retrospective implementation of SCâs March 11 judgement, which disallowed this classification of OBC candidates based on the salaries of parents employed in PSUs or the private sector.

Solicitor general Tushar Mehta requested a bench led by CJI Surya Kant to list the application seeking certain clarifications on the March 11 judgement in the Rohit Nathan case. This was opposed by advocate Varun Thakur, who said the law was settled by SC.

The SG said Centre was not seeking review or modification of the judgement but wanted to apprise the court of field-level difficulties in retrospective implementation.

The SG said this would require changing the status of older batches of creamy layer OBC candidates to non-creamy and warrant change in cadre, post and service in civil services. It would also necessitate corresponding changes for an equal number of candidates who had long been serving in a cadre and service like IFS, IAS and IPS, and result in chaos.

Mehta said he was only requesting early listing before a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and R Mahadevan.





CJI agreed to list the applications on Sept 1.

In its application, Centre said, âOn account of the serious challenges and implications with the implementation of the directions of SC, govt is committed to bring out a policy which will effectively address the observations made by SC, while also ensuring that the direct and indirect impact of the policy is fair and just.â

If the March 11 judgement is implemented without suitable policy intervention it will have a far-reaching impact on govt recruitments and admissions in higher education institutions undertaken by central as well as 18 state/UT govts, it said.

Govt said major bodies/employers â like Railways, banks, the department of posts and paramilitary â would also be flooded with hundreds of thousands of representations/litigations seeking retrospective reclassification of the creamy layer.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Following the Indra Sawhney judgement in 1992, govt had issued an office memorandum on Sept 8, 1993, prescribing the criteria for identifying the OBC creamy layer who would be excluded from reservation benefits.

In its March 11 judgement, SC had also observed that the determination of the creamy layer status must be based on the occupational categories specified in the 1993 office memorandum and the income of parents employed in private sector organisations could not automatically lead to the conclusion that the candidate belonged to the creamy layer.

World.title: Of 27 lakh ‘logical discrepancy’ deletions in West Bengal, only 7 lakh appealed
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a new twist to the simmering controversy over the West Bengal SIR, Supreme Court was informed Tuesday that against 27-lakh odd deletions from votersâ list because of âlogical discrepancyâ only seven lakh filed appeals seeking inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was informed by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan that of total 38.1 lakh appeals filed before the SIR appellate tribunals, an overwhelming 31 lakh were filed by those who challenged inclusion of names in the rolls claiming they were ineligible to be voters in Bengal.

Chunk of WB appeals was against inclusion

This was new information for SC, which was concerned by pendency of 37 lakh appeals, as 19 tribunals in last four months decided only 82,000 appeals.

The new turn means 20 lakh of 27-lakh-odd voters deleted for logical discrepancy have not appealed against being struck off the rolls during the SIR.

SC said a chunk of appeals was by those challenging inclusion. EC will give breakup differentiating those seeking inclusion from exclusion. Prioritising inclusion appeals would considerably reduce burden on tribunals, it said.

For petitioner Prasenjit Bose from Congress, advocates Gopal Sankaranarayanan and Neha Rathi alleged that bulk of appeals for exclusion/deletion have been filed by EC in a mechanical manner against orders of judicial officers who had directed inclusion of the names and these appeals should not be heard at all.





Sankaranarayanan said Kolkata and Howrah civic polls are due in Dec and at least appeals pertaining to these areas should be decided expeditiously so nobody gets disenfranchised illegally.

SC said its main concern was expeditious decision on appeals of disenfranchised people. It directed EC to respond with data on appeals pending after segregating them into two categories â those seeking inclusion and those seeking exclusion of names.

It asked EC to suggest a mechanism for speeding up disposal, including increasing the number of tribunals.

The bench also asked EC to detail steps taken to include names of those whose appeals had been allowed. EC said it was holding meetings with the acting CJ of Calcutta HC and would submit a proposal on expediting disposal.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Appearing for some petitioners, advocate Rauf Rahim said people whose names were deleted and whose appeals were pending should not be deprived of ration and benefits under the govt schemes.

Advocate Kalyan Bandopadhyay told the bench that in Murshidabad, many constituencies had voter deletions far exceeding winning margin, and alleged a particular community appeared to have been targeted through SIR. SC will hear issue again next week.

World.title: ‘Do we need a 4th-party audit?’ PM raps secretaries over quality of public projects
World.content:
Chairing the monthly Pragati meeting on Tuesday, PM Modi is learned to have told the top bureaucrats that such things are âunacceptableâ.

Couple speed of execution with uncompromising quality: PM

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: âDo we now need to go for a fourth-party audit?â PM Modi is learned to have asked secretaries at the Centre and chief secretaries in states while expressing concerns over reports of quality issues in construction and public projects. He made the observation that though âthird-partyâ audit of quality of works is a standard practice, this might not be working as expected.Chairing the monthly Pragati meeting on Tuesday, Modi is learned to have told the top bureaucrats that such things are âunacceptableâ and the system wonât work like this. World.title: Village in Rae Bareli tense after mud smeared on Ambedkar’s statue
World.content:
Baburiha village under the Gadganj police station limits in ​​Raebareli district remained tense on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) after unknown miscreants smeared mud and soot on a statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar on the intervening night, sparking widespread anger among villagers.

When villagers saw the condition of the statue in the morning, they demanded action against the culprits. “Baba Saheb’s followers and we, the local residents, are deeply angered. Unknown individuals took advantage of the darkness,” said Umesh Gautam, a local.

Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) Raebareli and Circle Officer (CO) Unchahar arrived at the scene, spoke to the angry villagers, calmed them down, and assured them of a fair investigation.

“Taking immediate cognisance of the incident, the Additional Superintendent of Police, Raebareli, the Circle Officer, Unchahar, along with the Gadganj police team, arrived at the scene and had the statue cleaned. CCTV footage from the surrounding area is being checked and necessary action is being taken. Peace and law and order are maintained at the scene,” reads a statement by the Raebareli police.

The police assured them of swift identification of the culprits and strict legal action. Police have been deployed in the village as a precautionary measure, and the situation is under control.

Congress party described the incident as a calculated nefarious strategy by the feudal forces to demoralise Dalits, adding that it is a pattern of vendetta against the community.
